title.zh: 卷57 列傳第22 盧思道 李孝貞 薛道衡
title.en: Volume 57 Biographies 22: Lu Sidao, Li Xiaozhen, Xue Daoheng
title.raw: 卷57 列傳第22 盧思道 李孝貞 薛道衡 Volume 57 Biographies 22: Lu Sidao, Li Xiaozhen, Xue Daoheng

sentences.zh: 盧思道從父兄昌衡

translations.literal: Lu Sidao's older cousin on his father's side, Changheng
translations.idiomatic: Changheng, Lu Sidao's paternal cousin

sentences.zh: 盧思道，字子行，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Sidao, style name Zixing, was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sidao, whose style was Zixing, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖陽烏，魏秘書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yangwu was Director of the Secretariat under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yangwu had served as Director of the Secretariat in Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父道亮，隱居不仕。

translations.literal: His father Daoliang lived in seclusion and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoliang had withdrawn from public life and never held office.

sentences.zh: 思道聰爽俊辯，通侻不羈。

translations.literal: Sidao was clever, sharp, handsome, and eloquent, open and unrestrained in manner.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao was bright, handsome, and quick-tongued, with an easy, unconstrained temperament.

sentences.zh: 年十六，遇中山劉松，松為人作碑銘，以示思道。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he met Liu Song of Zhongshan; Song had written an epitaph for someone and showed it to Sidao.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sixteen he met Liu Song of Zhongshan, who showed him an epitaph he had written for someone.

sentences.zh: 思道讀之，多所不解，於是感激，閉戶讀書，師事河間邢子才。

translations.literal: Sidao read it and understood little of it; stirred thereby, he shut his doors to study and took Xing Zicai of Hejian as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao read it and found much of it beyond him; stung to shame, he shut himself in to study and became a pupil of Xing Zicai of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 後思道複為文，以示劉松，松又不能甚解。

translations.literal: Later Sidao again wrote a piece and showed it to Liu Song, who in turn could not understand it very well.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sidao wrote another piece and showed it to Liu Song, who could no longer follow it very well either.

sentences.zh: 思道乃喟然歎曰：「學之有益，豈徒然哉！」

translations.literal: Sidao then sighed deeply and said, "Learning has its reward—was it all for nothing!"
translations.idiomatic: Sidao sighed and said, "So learning really does pay—this was no empty effort!"

sentences.zh: 因就魏收借異書，數年之間，才學兼著。

translations.literal: He then borrowed rare books from Wei Shou, and within a few years his talent and learning both became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed rare books from Wei Shou, and within a few years had won renown for both talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 然不持操行，好輕侮人。

translations.literal: Yet he did not maintain proper conduct and liked to treat others with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was careless of his conduct and prone to slighting others.

sentences.zh: 齊天保中，《魏史》未出，思道先已誦之，由是大被笞辱。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era of Qi, before the History of Wei was published, Sidao had already recited it, for which he was severely beaten and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi’s Tianbao reign, before the History of Wei was officially released, Sidao had already memorized it and was flogged and humiliated for it.

sentences.zh: 前後屢犯，因而不調。

translations.literal: He offended repeatedly, and as a result was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He kept giving offense, and was passed over for promotion.

sentences.zh: 其後左僕射楊遵彥薦之于朝，解褐司空行參軍，長兼員外散騎侍郎，直中書省。

translations.literal: Later the Left Vice Director Yang Zunyan recommended him to the court; he left the cloth and became Acting Attendant of the Minister of Works, concurrently Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and served in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Zunyan, Left Vice Director, recommended him at court; he entered office as Acting Attendant in the Ministry of Works, also served as Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and was posted to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文宣帝崩，當朝文士各作挽歌十首，擇其善者而用之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died, the literary men of the court each composed ten dirges, and the best were chosen for use.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan died, each leading writer at court submitted ten dirges, and the best lines were selected for the service.

sentences.zh: 魏收、陽休之、祖孝徵等不過得一二首，唯思道獨得八首。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Zu Xiaozheng, and the like had no more than one or two accepted; only Sidao alone had eight chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and Zu Xiaozheng each had only one or two pieces chosen, whereas Sidao alone had eight accepted.

sentences.zh: 故時人稱為「八米盧郎」。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time called him "Eight-Bushel Lu."
translations.idiomatic: People therefore nicknamed him "Eight-Bushel Lu."

sentences.zh: 後漏泄省中語，出為丞相西閤祭酒，曆太子舍人、司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Later, for leaking confidential talk from the Secretariat, he was sent out as Libationer of the Chancellor's Western Pavilion, and served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Recorder of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was demoted for leaking Secretariat secrets, becoming Libationer in the Chancellor’s Western Pavilion, and also served as Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Recorder under the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 每居官，多被譴辱。

translations.literal: Whenever he held office he was often rebuked and humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was repeatedly censured and shamed.

sentences.zh: 後以擅用庫錢，免歸於家。

translations.literal: Later, for misusing treasury funds, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed and sent home for unauthorized use of treasury funds.

sentences.zh: 嘗於薊北悵然感慨，為五言詩為見意，人以為工。

translations.literal: Once north of Ji he gave way to melancholy reflection and wrote a pentasyllabic poem to express his feelings; people considered it well wrought.
translations.idiomatic: Once, north of Ji, he gave way to melancholy and wrote a pentasyllabic poem to voice his mood; readers judged it finely done.

sentences.zh: 數年，複為京畿主簿，曆主客郎、給事黃門侍郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: After several years he again became Chief Clerk of the Capital Region, and served as Master of Guests, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and awaited imperial orders at the Forest of Letters.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he returned as Chief Clerk of the Capital Region, then served as Master of Guests and Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and was retained as a writer at the Forest of Letters.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授儀同三司，追赴長安，與同輩陽休之等數人作《聽蟬鳴篇》，思道所為，詞意清切，為時人所重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Sidao was granted the rank of Pillar of State, Third Order, and was summoned to Chang'an; with several peers including Yang Xiuzhi he composed "On Hearing the Cicadas"; Sidao's piece, in language clear and keen, was highly valued by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Sidao was made Pillar of State, Third Order, and summoned to Chang'an; he and peers such as Yang Xiuzhi wrote "On Hearing the Cicadas," and Sidao's contribution, lucid and piercing in diction, won great esteem.

sentences.zh: 新野庾信遍覽諸同作者，而深歎美之。

translations.literal: Yu Xin of Xinye read through all the co-authors' works and sighed deeply in admiration of his.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin of Xinye read all the contributions and sighed in deep admiration of Sidao's.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以母疾還鄉，遇同郡祖英伯及從兄昌期、宋護等舉兵作亂，思道預焉。

translations.literal: Before long, returning home because his mother was ill, he encountered Zu Yingbo of his commandery and his cousin Changqi, Song Hu, and others raising troops in rebellion; Sidao took part.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he went home because his mother was ill and became involved when Zu Yingbo of his commandery, his cousin Changqi, Song Hu, and others rose in arms; Sidao joined them.

sentences.zh: 周遣柱國宇文神舉討平之，罪當法，已在死中。

translations.literal: Zhou sent the Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju to suppress them; the crime called for the law, and he was already as good as dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju to put down the revolt; the offense merited execution, and Sidao was already as good as dead.

sentences.zh: 神舉素聞其名，引出之，令作露布。

translations.literal: Shenju had long heard his name, had him brought out, and ordered him to compose a victory proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Shenju had long known his reputation, had him brought forth, and ordered him to draft a victory proclamation.

sentences.zh: 思道援筆立成，文無加點，神舉嘉而宥之。

translations.literal: Sidao took up the brush and finished at once, the text needing not a single correction; Shenju praised him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao wrote it at a stroke, flawless without emendation; Shenju was pleased and spared him.

sentences.zh: 後除掌教上士。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Senior Master of Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Senior Master of Instruction.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，遷武陽太守，非其好也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Sidao was transferred to be Administrator of Wuyang—not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Sidao was moved to Administrator of Wuyang, a post that did not suit him.

sentences.zh: 為《孤鴻賦》以寄其情曰：

translations.literal: He wrote "Rhapsody on a Lone Goose" to lodge his feelings, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Rhapsody on a Lone Goose" to express his feelings, which read:

sentences.zh: 餘志學之歲，自鄉里游京師，便見識知音，曆受群公之眷。

translations.literal: In the year I set my heart on learning, I left my village for the capital and at once found those who knew and understood me, receiving the favor of many lords in turn.
translations.idiomatic: In the year I began serious study I left my home for the capital, where I soon found patrons who understood me and won the regard of many great men in turn.

sentences.zh: 年登弱冠，甫就朝列，談者過誤，遂竊虛名。

translations.literal: When I reached twenty I had just entered the court ranks; talkers erred in praise, and I thus stole an empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: By twenty I had barely joined the court; gossipers overrated me, and I came by a hollow fame.

sentences.zh: 通人楊令君、邢特進已下，皆分庭致禮，倒屣相接，翦拂吹噓，長其光價。

translations.literal: Men of insight such as Lord Yang, Special Advance Xing, and those below them all received me as an equal, rushed out with shoes reversed to greet me, trimmed and puffed me up, and raised my market price.
translations.idiomatic: Learned men from Lord Yang and Special Advance Xing downward all treated me as an equal, hurried out shoeless to welcome me, polished my reputation, and inflated my standing.

sentences.zh: 而才本駑拙，性實疏懶，勢利貨殖，淡然不營。

translations.literal: Yet my talent was by nature dull and clumsy, my disposition truly lax and indolent; profit and gain I regarded with detachment and did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my gifts were naturally mediocre, my nature truly slack and indolent; I cared nothing for profit or gain.

sentences.zh: 雖籠絆朝市且三十載，而獨往之心未始去懷抱也。

translations.literal: Though bound to court and market for nearly thirty years, the heart that goes its own way never left my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court held me fast for nearly thirty years, the wish to go my own way never left me.

sentences.zh: 攝生舛和，有少氣疾。

translations.literal: In tending my life I fell out of harmony and suffered a slight disorder of the breath.
translations.idiomatic: My regimen had gone awry, and I suffered a mild disorder of the breath.

sentences.zh: 分符坐嘯，作守東原。

translations.literal: I received the tally and sat ruling with a whistle, becoming guardian of the eastern plain.
translations.idiomatic: I took office with seal in hand and became magistrate of the eastern plain.

sentences.zh: 洪河之湄，沃野彌望，囂務既屏，魚鳥為鄰。

translations.literal: On the banks of the mighty river, fertile fields stretched as far as the eye could see; clamor of office was shut away, and fish and birds were my neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: Along the great river lay rich fields without end; the noise of office fell away, and fish and birds were my companions.

sentences.zh: 有離群之鴻，為羅者所獲，野人馴養，貢之于餘。

translations.literal: There was a goose that had left the flock, taken by a fowler; a countryman tamed it and presented it to me.
translations.idiomatic: A goose that had strayed from the flock was caught by a fowler; a rustic tamed it and presented it to me.

sentences.zh: 置諸池庭，朝夕賞玩，既用銷憂，兼以輕疾。

translations.literal: I placed it in the pool and courtyard, admiring it morning and evening; it both dispelled sorrow and eased my slight illness.
translations.idiomatic: I kept it in the pool and courtyard and admired it morning and evening; it eased my cares and lightened my mild ailment.

sentences.zh: 《大易》稱「鴻漸于陸」，羽儀盛也。

translations.literal: The Great Changes says, "The goose gradually advances upon the land"—its feathered regalia is splendid.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "The goose gradually reaches the shore"—a splendid display of pinions.

sentences.zh: 《揚子》曰「鴻飛冥冥」，騫翥高也。

translations.literal: Master Yang says, "The goose flies in the deep gloom"—soaring high aloft.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong says, "The goose flies in the dim distance"—soaring to great heights.

sentences.zh: 《淮南》雲「東歸碣石」，違溽暑也。

translations.literal: The Huainanzi says, "It returns east to Jieshi"—fleeing the sweltering heat.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainanzi says it "returns east to Jieshi," fleeing the oppressive summer.

sentences.zh: 平子賦曰「南寓衡陽」，避祁寒也。

translations.literal: Pingzi's rhapsody says, "It lodges south at Hengyang"—avoiding severe cold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng's rhapsody says it "sojourns south at Hengyang," shunning bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 若其雅步清音，遠心高致，鵷鸞以降，罕見其儔，而鎩翮牆陰，偶影獨立，唼喋粃粺，雞鶩為伍，不亦傷乎！

translations.literal: In its elegant gait and clear cry, its far-ranging mind and lofty bearing, among yuanluan and phoenixes downward one rarely finds its peer—yet with broken pinions in the wall's shade, standing alone with only its shadow, pecking chaff and bran among chickens and ducks: is that not grievous!
translations.idiomatic: In grace of step and clarity of call, in lofty spirit and distant aim, among the phoenix-kind one seldom finds its equal—yet with wings clipped in a courtyard corner, standing alone with only its shadow, pecking scraps beside chickens and ducks: how pitiful!

sentences.zh: 餘五十之年，忽焉已至，永言身事，慨然多緒，乃為之賦，聊以自慰雲。

translations.literal: My fiftieth year has suddenly arrived; speaking long of my life's affairs, I am moved to many feelings, and therefore composed this rhapsody, merely to console myself.
translations.idiomatic: My fiftieth year has come all at once; reflecting on my life's course, I am stirred to many thoughts, and so I wrote this rhapsody simply to comfort myself.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: The words say:
translations.idiomatic: The text runs:

sentences.zh: 惟此孤鴻，擅奇羽蟲，實稟清高之氣，遠生遼碣之東。

translations.literal: This lone goose alone among feathered creatures claims wonder; it truly partakes of lofty, pure qi, born far away east of Liaojie.
translations.idiomatic: This lone goose, singular among winged creatures, truly bears a lofty, pure nature, born far away east of the frontier passes.

sentences.zh: 氄毛將落，和鳴順風，壯冰雲厚，矯翅排空。

translations.literal: Down feathers about to shed, it harmonizes its cry with the wind; thick ice and clouds mass, and it straightens its wings to pierce the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Its down about to molt, it sings in harmony with the wind; where ice and clouds lie heavy, it spreads its wings and cleaves the sky.

sentences.zh: 出島嶼之綿邈，犯霜露之溟濛，驚絓魚之密網，畏落雁之虛弓。

translations.literal: It leaves the far-stretching isles, braves the misty frost and dew, startles at the fish-trapper's close nets, and fears the empty bow that fells the falling goose.
translations.idiomatic: It leaves distant isles behind, faces mist and frost, starts at the fisher's close-set nets, and dreads the bow that brings down the migrating goose.

sentences.zh: 若其斗柄東指，女夷司月，乃遙集於寒門，遂輕舉于玄闕。

translations.literal: When the Dipper's handle points east and Nüyi governs the moon, it gathers from afar at the Cold Gate and lightly rises to the Dark Tower.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dipper turns east and the moon-maid takes charge of the month, it gathers far off at the Cold Gate and lightly ascends to the Dark Tower.

sentences.zh: 至如天高氣肅，搖落在時，既嘯儔於淮浦，亦弄吭于江湄。

translations.literal: As when heaven is high and the air stern and leaves fall in season, it cries with its fellows on the Huai shore and also trills its throat on the river's edge.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven stands high and the air turns crisp and leaves fall in season, it calls with its flock along the Huai and sings along the riverbanks.

sentences.zh: 摩赤霄以淩厲，乘丹氣之威夷，逆商飆之嫋嫋，玩陽景之遲遲。

translations.literal: It brushes the crimson empyrean in fierce ascent, rides the august power of cinnabar qi, meets the swirling autumn blast, and delights in the lingering sun's glow.
translations.idiomatic: It brushes the crimson sky in bold flight, rides the power of the red ether, meets the swirling autumn wind, and lingers in the slow-setting sun.

sentences.zh: 彭蠡方春，洞庭初綠，理翮整翰，群浮侶浴。

translations.literal: When Penglai is in spring and Dongting first turns green, it arranges pinions and straightens quills; the flock floats and companions bathe.
translations.idiomatic: When spring comes to Poyang and Dongting first greens, it preens its wings; the flock floats together and bathes as one.

sentences.zh: 振雪羽而臨風，掩霜毛而候旭，饜江湖之菁藻，飫原野之菽粟。

translations.literal: It shakes snow-white feathers facing the wind, covers frost-touched down awaiting dawn, sates itself on the rivers' and lakes' fine plants, and feasts on the wild fields' beans and grain.
translations.idiomatic: It shakes snow-white plumes in the wind, folds frost-gray down to await the dawn, feasts on the lush plants of rivers and lakes, and fills itself on beans and grain of the open country.

sentences.zh: 行離離而高逝，響噰噰而相續，潔齊國之冰紈，皓密山之華玉。

translations.literal: It goes far off in lofty flight, its calls echoing one after another, pure as Qi state's ice-white silk, bright as Mishan's splendid jade.
translations.idiomatic: It departs in lofty flight, its calls echoing on and on, pure as the ice-silk of Qi, bright as the fine jade of Mishan.

sentences.zh: 若乃晨沐清露，安趾徐步；

translations.literal: At dawn it bathes in clear dew and sets its feet at ease in slow steps;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn it bathes in clear dew and walks at ease with measured steps;

sentences.zh: 夕息芳洲，延頸乘流；

translations.literal: at evening it rests on a fragrant islet, stretching its neck to ride the current;
translations.idiomatic: at evening it rests on a fragrant islet, stretching its neck upon the current;

sentences.zh: 違寒競逐，浮沅水宿；

translations.literal: fleeing cold it races in pursuit, floats on the Yuan and lodges upon the waters;
translations.idiomatic: fleeing the cold it races in pursuit, drifts on the Yuan and roosts upon the stream;

sentences.zh: 避暑言歸，絕漠雲飛。

translations.literal: escaping summer heat it speaks of returning home, flying through clouds beyond the desert.
translations.idiomatic: shunning the summer heat it turns homeward, flying through clouds across the desert.

sentences.zh: 望玄鵠而為侶，比硃鷺而相依，倦天衢之冥漠，降河渚之芳菲。

translations.literal: It looks to the dark swan as companion, ranks itself with the vermilion egret in mutual reliance, wearies of the dark vastness of heaven's road, and descends to the river islet's fragrant blooms.
translations.idiomatic: It takes the dark swan for companion, keeps company with the vermilion egret, wearies of heaven's trackless gloom, and alights on the fragrant river islet.

sentences.zh: 忽值羅人設網，虞者懸機，永辭寥廓，蹈跡重圍。

translations.literal: Suddenly it meets the net-setter's snare, the gamekeeper's sprung trap; forever it leaves the vast expanse and treads within layered enclosures.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the fowler sets his net, the huntsman springs his trap; it bids farewell forever to the open sky and walks within a double cage.

sentences.zh: 始則窘束籠樊，憂憚刀俎，靡軀絕命，恨失其所。

translations.literal: At first it is cramped and bound in cage and pen, fearful of knife and chopping-block, willing to give body and life, grieving that it has lost its place.
translations.idiomatic: At first cramped in cage and pen, it dreads knife and block, would yield body and life, and grieves to have lost its proper realm.

sentences.zh: 終乃馴狎園庭，棲托池禦，稻粱為惠，恣其容與。

translations.literal: In the end it grows tame in garden and court, lodges in the imperial pool, takes grain and millet as bounty, and roams at ease as it will.
translations.idiomatic: In time it grows tame in garden and court, lodges in the palace pool, accepts grain as a gift, and wanders at ease.

sentences.zh: 於是翕羽宛頸，屏氣銷聲，滅煙霞之高想，悶江海之幽情。

translations.literal: Thereupon it folds its feathers and bends its neck, holds its breath and silences its cry, extinguishes lofty thoughts of mist and rosy clouds, and stifles the deep feeling of rivers and seas.
translations.idiomatic: Then it folds its wings and bows its neck, holds its breath and stills its cry, quenches lofty dreams of mist and glow, and smothers the deep longing of rivers and sea.

sentences.zh: 何時驤首奮翼，上淩太清，騫翥鼓舞，遠薄層城。

translations.literal: When will it toss its head and beat its wings, ascend to pierce the Grand Clarity, soar and dance in flight, and approach from afar the layered walls?
translations.idiomatic: When will it toss its head and spread its wings, soar to the highest heaven, rise in exultant flight, and reach the distant tiered walls?

sentences.zh: 惡禽視而不貴，小鳥顧而相輕，安控地而無恥，豈沖天之複榮！

translations.literal: Vile birds look but do not esteem it; small birds glance and likewise despise it—content to be held to earth without shame: how could piercing heaven be glory again!
translations.idiomatic: Base birds look on without respect; small birds glance and scorn it—content to be held to earth without shame: what glory could there be in piercing heaven again!

sentences.zh: 若夫圖南之羽，偉而去羨，棲睫之蟲，微而不賤，各遂性於天壤，弗企懷以交戰。

translations.literal: As for the wing that charts the south—great and without envy; the insect that dwells on an eyelash—small yet not base: each follows its nature between heaven and earth and does not harbor warring ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: The bird that charts the south is great yet envies none; the mite on an eyelash is tiny yet not despised: each follows its nature under heaven and does not harbor warring desires.

sentences.zh: 不聽咸池之樂，不饗太牢之薦，匹晨雞而共飲，偶野鳧以同膳。

translations.literal: It does not hear the music of Xianchi, does not feast on the great offering, pairs with the morning cock to drink together, and joins the wild duck in the same meal.
translations.idiomatic: It hears not the music of Xianchi, tastes not the grand sacrifice, drinks beside the morning cock, and shares its meal with the wild drake.

sentences.zh: 匪揚聲以顯聞，寧校體而求見，聊寓形乎沼沚，且夷心於溏澱。

translations.literal: It does not raise its voice to win renown, but would rather compare its body to seek notice; for now it lodges its form in marsh and islet, and levels its heart in muddy shallows.
translations.idiomatic: It does not cry out for fame, but would rather measure its frame to be seen; for now it lodges in marsh and pool, and quiets its heart in muddy shallows.

sentences.zh: 齊榮辱以晏如，承君子之余眄。

translations.literal: It makes honor and disgrace equal and remains serene, receiving the gentleman's lingering glance.
translations.idiomatic: It treats honor and shame alike and stays serene, enjoying the gentleman's kindly regard.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以母老，表請解職，優詔許之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, because his mother was old, he memorialized requesting release from office, and an excellent edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang reign, citing his mother's age, he petitioned to resign, and the emperor graciously approved.

sentences.zh: 思道自恃才地，多所陵轢，由是官途淪滯。

translations.literal: Sidao relied on his talent and background and often bullied others; for this reason his official career sank into stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao trusted in his talent and pedigree and often rode roughshod over others, and his career therefore languished.

sentences.zh: 既而又著《勞生論》，指切當時，其詞曰：

translations.literal: Thereafter he again wrote "On the Toils of Life," pointing sharply at his own time; the words say:
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote "On the Toils of Life," a pointed critique of his age, which begins:

sentences.zh: 《莊子》曰：「大塊勞我以生。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzi says, "The great clod labors me with life."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi says, "The great clod burdens me with life."

sentences.zh: 誠哉斯言也！

translations.literal: Truly are these words!
translations.idiomatic: How true those words are!

sentences.zh: 餘年五十，羸老雲至，追惟疇昔，勤矣厥生。

translations.literal: I am fifty years old; frailty and old age come like clouds; looking back on days past, how toilsome has been this life of mine.
translations.idiomatic: I am fifty; frailty and age gather like clouds; looking back on the past, how laborious my life has been.

sentences.zh: 乃著茲論，因言時雲爾。

translations.literal: Therefore I composed this treatise, speaking of the times as follows.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore wrote this essay to speak of the times as follows.

sentences.zh: 罷郡屏居，有客造餘者，少選之頃，盱衡而言曰：「生者天地之大德，人者有生之最靈，所以作配兩儀，稱貴群品，妍蚩愚智之辯，天懸壤隔，行己立身之異，入海頓山。

translations.literal: Dismissed from my commandery and living in seclusion, a guest came to visit me; after a brief wait he squared his shoulders and said, "Life is the great virtue of heaven and earth; man is the most spiritual among the living, therefore paired with the Two Principles and called noble among all kinds. The distinction of fair and foul, foolish and wise, hangs between heaven and earth; differences in conduct and standing are as vast as entering the sea or halting a mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving my post and living in retirement, a visitor called; presently he drew himself up and said, "Life is heaven and earth's greatest virtue; man is the most spirited of living things, paired with yin and yang and honored above all creatures. The gap between beauty and ugliness, folly and wisdom, is as wide as heaven from earth; differences in conduct and station are as vast as the sea or a mountain's halt.

sentences.zh: 今吾子生於右地，九葉卿族，天授俊才，萬夫所仰，學綜流略，慕孔門之游、夏，辭窮麗則，擬漢日之卿、雲。

translations.literal: Now you, sir, were born in the right land, a ministerial clan of nine generations, heaven-endowed with outstanding talent admired by ten thousand men; your learning embraces the currents and outlines, you emulate You and Xia of Confucius's gate, your phrasing exhausts beautiful rules, and you rival Qing and Yun of Han days.
translations.idiomatic: You, sir, were born in a noble region, of a ministerial house nine generations deep, gifted by heaven with talent ten thousand men admire; your learning spans the classics, you emulate Ziyou and Zixia of Confucius's school, your style exhausts elegance, and you rival Sima Xiangru and Yang Yun of Han.

sentences.zh: 行藏有節，進退以禮，不諂不驕，無慍無懌，偃仰貴賤之間，從容語默之際，何其裕也！

translations.literal: In action and withdrawal you have measure, in advance and retreat you follow ritual, neither fawning nor proud, without anger or resentment; between bowing high and low, in ease of speech and silence—how ample you are!
translations.idiomatic: You act and withdraw with measure, advance and retire by ritual, neither fawning nor arrogant, free of anger and resentment; whether bowing high or low, in speech or silence—how spacious your bearing!

sentences.zh: 下走所欣羡焉。」

translations.literal: This humble runner greatly admires you."
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant admires this greatly."

sentences.zh: 餘莞爾而笑曰：「未之思乎？

translations.literal: I smiled gently and said, "Have you not thought it through?
translations.idiomatic: I smiled and said, "Have you not thought this through?

sentences.zh: 何所言之過也！

translations.literal: How excessive your words are!
translations.idiomatic: How far your praise goes!

sentences.zh: 子其清耳，請為左右陳之。

translations.literal: Clear your ears, sir, and allow me to set it forth for those beside you.
translations.idiomatic: Listen closely, and let me explain it for you.

sentences.zh: 夫人之生也，皆未若無生。

translations.literal: As for human life, none is better than not to have been born.
translations.idiomatic: Of all human conditions, none is better than never to have been born.

sentences.zh: 在余之生，勞亦勤止，紈綺之年，伏膺教義，規行矩步，從善而登。

translations.literal: In my life, toil has also been ceaseless; in the years of silk and brocade I bowed to received teaching, walked by compass and square, and climbed by following the good.
translations.idiomatic: In my own life, labor has never ceased; in my youth I embraced instruction, walked by the rule, and rose by following what was right.

sentences.zh: 巾冠之後，濯纓受署，韁鎖仁義，籠絆朝市。

translations.literal: After cap and scarf I rinsed my tassel and accepted appointment, bridled by benevolence and righteousness, caged by court and market.
translations.idiomatic: After I came of age I rinsed my cap-tassel and took office, bridled by benevolence and righteousness, bound to court and marketplace.

sentences.zh: 失翹陸之本性，喪江湖之遠情，淪此風波，溺於倒躓，憂勞總至，事非一緒。

translations.literal: I lost the nature of soaring on land, abandoned the distant feeling of rivers and lakes, sank into these waves, drowned in stumbling; care and toil arrived together, and causes were not of one kind.
translations.idiomatic: I lost the nature of one who soars on land, forsook the freedom of rivers and lakes, was swallowed by these storms and drowned in missteps; cares and labors came all at once, and for many reasons.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why so?

sentences.zh: 地胄高華，既致嫌于管庫，才識美茂，亦受嫉於愚庸。

translations.literal: A pedigree high and splendid already draws suspicion from clerks and storekeepers; talent and insight fine and lush also draw envy from the foolish and mediocre.
translations.idiomatic: A lofty pedigree already draws suspicion from petty officials; fine talent and insight also draw envy from the dull and mediocre.

sentences.zh: 篤學強記，聾瞽於焉側目，清言河瀉，木訥所以疚心。

translations.literal: Deep learning and strong memory make the deaf and blind cast sidelong glances; clear talk that pours like a river makes the wooden and tongue-tied feel pangs of heart.
translations.idiomatic: Deep learning and a keen memory make the ignorant glare sidelong; eloquent speech flowing like a river makes the tongue-tied writhe with shame.

sentences.zh: 豈徒蟲惜春漿，鴟吝腐鼠，相江都而永歎，傅長沙而不歸，固亦魯值臧倉，楚逢靳尚，趙壹為之哀歌，張升於是慟哭。

translations.literal: Is it only that insects begrudge spring sap, or ospreys begrudge rotten rats; that one sighs forever like the Chancellor of Jiangdu, or is exiled to Changsha and does not return? Surely also in Lu one meets Zang Cang, in Chu one meets Jin Shang; Zhao Yi sang a lament for this, and Zhang Sheng wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that insects begrudge spring sap or ospreys begrudge rotten rats; not only that one sighs like Dong Zhongshu of Jiangdu or is banished to Changsha like Jia Yi and never returns—one also meets a Zang Cang in Lu, a Jin Shang in Chu; Zhao Yi sang his lament for this, and Zhang Sheng wept.

sentences.zh: 有齊之季，不遇休明，申脰就鞅，屏跡無地。

translations.literal: In the late age of Qi one did not meet enlightened rule; one stretched one's neck to the yoke and had nowhere to hide one's traces.
translations.idiomatic: In the last days of Qi one found no enlightened age; one bowed the neck to the yoke and had nowhere to hide.

sentences.zh: 段珪、張讓，金貝是視，賈謐、郭淮，腥臊可饜。

translations.literal: Duan Gui and Zhang Rang looked only to gold and shells; Jia Mi and Guo Huai could be sated with stench and filth.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Gui and Zhang Rang cared only for gold; Jia Mi and Guo Huai were glutted with corruption.

sentences.zh: 淫刑以逞，禍近池魚，耳聽惡來之讒，足踐龍逢之血。

translations.literal: Licentious punishments were indulged; disaster neared the fish in the moat; the ear heard the slander of Fei Lian, the foot trod the blood of Long Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Cruel punishments ran riot; disaster reached even the fish in the moat; men's ears heard slander like Fei Lian's, their feet trod blood like Long Feng's.

sentences.zh: 周氏末葉，仍值僻王，斂笏升階，汗流浹背，莒客之踵躋焦原，匹茲非險，齊人之手執馬尾，方此未危。

translations.literal: In the last leaves of Zhou one still met a perverse king; gathering one's tablet and ascending the steps, sweat streamed down the back—the Juchen guest's heel treading Jiaoyuan was not as perilous as this; the Qi man's hand holding the horse's tail was not yet as dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou's last days one still served a wayward king; ascending the steps with tablet in hand, sweat soaked one's back—the peril when a Juchen envoy trod Jiaoyuan was nothing beside this; the danger when a man of Qi seized a horse's tail was mild by comparison.

sentences.zh: 若乃羊腸、句注之道，據鞍振策，武落、雞田之外，櫛風沐雨，三旬九食，不敢稱弊，此之為役，蓋其小小者耳。

translations.literal: As for the roads of Yangchang and Gouzhu, gripping the saddle and flourishing the whip; beyond Wuluo and Jitian, combing the wind and bathing in rain, nine meals in thirty days, not daring to call it hardship—such service is but the smallest of small things.
translations.idiomatic: The passes of Yangchang and Gouzhu, riding hard with whip in hand; beyond Wuluo and Jitian, wind-combed and rain-soaked, nine meals in thirty days without daring to call it hardship—such labors were but trifles.

sentences.zh: 今泰運肇開，四門以穆，冕旒司契於上，夔、龍佐命於下，岐伯、善卷，恥徇幽憂，卞隨、務光，悔從木石。

translations.literal: Now the great fortune has newly opened, the four gates are serene; the imperial crown holds the tally above, Kui and Long assist the mandate below; Qibo and Shan Juan would be ashamed to follow dark sorrow, Bian Sui and Wu Guang would regret keeping to wood and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Now a great age has dawned, the four gates stand serene; the emperor holds the tally on high, worthy ministers assist below; Qibo and Shan Juan would blush to nurse private grief, Bian Sui and Wu Guang would regret hiding like wood and stone.

sentences.zh: 餘年在秋方，已迫知命，情禮宜退，不獲晏安。

translations.literal: My surplus years are in the autumn quarter; already I press upon knowing destiny; feeling and ritual ought to withdraw—I do not obtain peaceful ease.
translations.idiomatic: I am in the autumn of my life, already nearing the age when one knows one's allotted span; sentiment and propriety call for stepping back, and I cannot find rest.

sentences.zh: 一葉從風，無損鄧林之攢植，雙鳧退飛，不虧渤澥之游泳。

translations.literal: One leaf follows the wind—no harm to the dense planting of the Deng Forest; twin ducks retreat in flight—no loss to swimming in the Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: A single leaf blown by the wind does not diminish the great grove of Deng; two wild ducks flying away do not empty the vast waters of the Bohai.

sentences.zh: 耕田鑿井，晚息晨興，候南山之朝雲，攬北堂之明月。

translations.literal: Plowing fields and digging wells, resting at evening and rising at dawn, awaiting the morning clouds of South Mountain, embracing the bright moon of the north hall.
translations.idiomatic: I plow and dig wells, rise at dawn and rest at dusk, watch the morning clouds over the southern hills, and enjoy the moonlight in my northern hall.

sentences.zh: 氾勝九穀之書，觀其節制，崔實四人之令，奉以周旋。

translations.literal: Fan Sheng's book on the nine grains—observing its regulations; Cui Shi's ordinance for the four seasons—following it in daily round.
translations.idiomatic: I study Fan Sheng's treatise on the nine grains and heed its seasonal rules, and I live by Cui Shi's four-seasons ordinance in my daily round.

sentences.zh: 晨荷蓑笠，白屋黃冠之伍，夕談穀稼，沾體塗足之倫。

translations.literal: Morning: bearing straw cloak and rain hat among white-hut and yellow-cap folk; evening: talking of grain crops with those whose bodies are stained and feet muddied.
translations.idiomatic: In the morning I shoulder hoe and cloak among simple farmers in white cottages; in the evening I talk crops with neighbors whose clothes and feet are caked with mud.

sentences.zh: 濁酒盈樽，高歌滿席，恍兮惚兮，天地一指。

translations.literal: Muddy wine filling the goblet, lofty songs filling the mats—vague and dim, heaven and earth as one finger.
translations.idiomatic: Rough wine fills the cup and hearty songs fill the mat until, in a daze, heaven and earth seem but a single span.

sentences.zh: 此野人之樂也，子或以是羨餘乎？」

translations.literal: This is the wild man's joy—do you perhaps envy me for this?"
translations.idiomatic: That is the rustic's delight—perhaps you envy me for it?"

sentences.zh: 客曰：「吾子之事，既聞之矣。

translations.literal: The guest said: 'Your lordship's affairs—I have already heard of them.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said, "I have already heard your account, sir.

sentences.zh: 他人有心，又請論其梗概。」

translations.literal: Others have their hearts—again I ask to discuss the general outline."
translations.idiomatic: Others have their own concerns; please also give me the gist of theirs."

sentences.zh: 餘答曰：「雲飛泥沉，卑高異等，圓行方止，動息殊致。

translations.literal: I answered: 'Clouds fly and mud sinks—low and high are different ranks; the round moves, the square stops—movement and rest are separate modes.
translations.idiomatic: I replied, "Clouds rise and mud sinks—high and low are not the same rank; what is round rolls on and what is square stays put—motion and rest follow different laws.

sentences.zh: 是以摩霄運海，輕罻羅於藪澤，五衢四照，忽斤斧于山林。

translations.literal: Therefore those who soar to the sky and sail the sea lightly cast nets in marsh and lake; where five crossroads shine in all directions, suddenly hatchets fall in mountain forests.
translations.idiomatic: Those who range the heavens and cross the seas will still cast a light net in some marsh; where every road is bright with traffic, the axe suddenly falls in the hills.

sentences.zh: 餘晚值昌辰，遂其弱尚，觀人事之隕獲，睹時路之邅危。

translations.literal: I lately met a flourishing age and followed my weaker inclinations, observing the fall and gain of human affairs, witnessing the perils and dangers of the times.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately lived in a prosperous age yet clung to my modest tastes, watching how men rise and fall and how perilous the roads of the times can be.

sentences.zh: 玄冬修夜，靜言長想，可以累歎悼心，流涕酸鼻。

translations.literal: Deep winter, long night—in quiet I think long: one may accumulate sighs to mourn the heart, shed tears and sour the nose.
translations.idiomatic: On deep-winter nights, when I sit in silence and think at length, sighs pile up in my heart and tears sting my nose.

sentences.zh: 人之百年，脆促已甚，奔駒流電，不可為辭。

translations.literal: Man's hundred years—brittle and brief already beyond measure; galloping colt and flowing lightning—nothing can be put into words.
translations.idiomatic: A human life of a hundred years is frail and short beyond telling—like a galloping horse or a flash of lightning, it defies words.

sentences.zh: 顧慕周章，數紀之內，窮通榮辱，事無足道。

translations.literal: Looking back in anxious yearning, within several decades—poverty and wealth, glory and shame—nothing worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back in restless longing, I find that within a few decades poverty and wealth, honor and disgrace, are scarcely worth mentioning.

sentences.zh: 而有識者鮮，無識者多，褊隘凡近，輕險躁薄。

translations.literal: Yet those with understanding are few, those without understanding many—narrow, petty, vulgar and near, light, dangerous, rash and shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Men of insight are few and the ignorant many; most are narrow, vulgar, reckless, and shallow.

sentences.zh: 居家則人面獸心，不孝不義，出門則諂諛讒佞，無愧無恥。

translations.literal: At home then human face but beast heart—unfilial and unrighteous; going out then fawning and slanderous, flatterer and sycophant—without shame or sense of disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: At home they wear a human face but harbor a beast's heart, failing in filial piety and righteousness; abroad they fawn, slander, and flatter, without shame or decency.

sentences.zh: 退身知足，忘伯陽之炯戒，陳力就列，棄周任之格言。

translations.literal: Retreating and knowing sufficiency—they forget Boyang's bright warning; exerting strength and taking one's place—they abandon the maxims of Zhou Ren.
translations.idiomatic: They forget Laozi's teaching to withdraw and be content, and they cast aside the Zhou maxim that one should serve only while able.

sentences.zh: 悠悠遠古，斯患已積，迄於近代，此蠹尤深。

translations.literal: From distant antiquity this trouble has piled up; down to recent times this pest is especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: This evil has accumulated since remote antiquity, and in recent times the rot has grown especially deep.

sentences.zh: 範卿捴讓之風，搢紳不嗣，《夏書》昏墊之罪，執政所安。

translations.literal: Fan Qing's yielding manner—gentry do not inherit; the crime of delusion in the Xia Documents—those in power rest easy in it.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit of humble yielding that Fan Li embodied is no longer passed on among officials, while the deluded conduct condemned in the Documents of Xia is treated as harmless by those in power.

sentences.zh: 朝露未晞，小車盈董、石之巷，夕陽且落，皁蓋填閻、竇之裡。

translations.literal: Before morning dew dries, small carriages fill the lanes of Dong and Shi; as sunset approaches, black canopies cram the quarters of Yan and Dou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the morning dew has dried, carriages crowd the lanes of the Dong and Shi mansions; as the sun sets, black-canopied coaches pack the wards of Yan and Dou.

sentences.zh: 皆如脂如韋，俯僂匍匐，啖惡求媚，舐痔自親。

translations.literal: All are like grease, like leather—bowing low, crawling on knees, eating foulness to seek favor, licking hemorrhoids to draw close.
translations.idiomatic: They are supple as grease or leather, bowing and crawling, swallowing filth to win favor and fawning in the vilest ways to draw near.

sentences.zh: 美言諂笑，助其愉樂，詐泣佞哀，恤其喪紀。

translations.literal: Fine words and flattery smiles to aid his pleasure; false weeping and sycophantic grief to comfort his mourning.
translations.idiomatic: With honeyed words and flattering smiles they heighten his pleasures; with feigned tears and hypocritical sorrow they console his bereavements.

sentences.zh: 近通旨酒，遠貢文蛇，豔姬美女，委如脫屣，金銑玉華，棄同遺跡。

translations.literal: Near: sending fine wine; far: offering tribute serpents—beautiful concubines and lovely women cast off like removing shoes; golden ornament and jade splendor abandoned like discarded traces.
translations.idiomatic: They send fine wine from nearby and tribute serpents from afar, casting off beautiful women as one kicks off a shoe and discarding gold and jade as though they were nothing.

sentences.zh: 及鄧通失路，一簪之賄無餘，梁冀就誅，五侯之貴將起。

translations.literal: When Deng Tong lost his way, not a hairpin's bribe remained; when Liang Ji was executed, the nobility of the Five Marquises was about to rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Tong fell, not even a hairpin's worth of his gifts remained; when Liang Ji was executed, the power of the Five Marquises was already rising.

sentences.zh: 向之求官買職，晚謁晨趨，刺促望塵之舊游，伊優上堂之夜客，始則亡魂褫魄，若牛兄之遇獸，心戰色沮，似葉公之見龍；

translations.literal: Formerly those seeking office and buying posts, evening visits and morning dashes, the old associates who hurried looking at dust—night guests who fawned at the upper hall—at first lost soul and stripped spirit, like the ox brother meeting beasts; heart battled and color fell, like Lord Ye seeing the dragon;
translations.idiomatic: Those who once bought office and scurried to pay court—old hangers-on who raced after carriage dust and fawning night visitors at the great man's door—at first lost their wits in terror, like a man who meets a beast, or turned pale as Lord Ye at the sight of a dragon;

sentences.zh: 俄而抵掌揚眉，高視闊步，結侶棄廉公之第，攜手哭聖卿之門。

translations.literal: Suddenly then clapping hands and raising brows, looking down from on high with broad steps, forming companions to abandon the Marquis of Lian's mansion, joining hands to weep at Marquis Sheng's gate.
translations.idiomatic: then suddenly they clap their hands and swagger, strut with lofty air, band together to shun the house of Lord Lian, and join hands to mourn at Lord Sheng's gate.

sentences.zh: 華轂生塵，來如激矢，雀羅暫設，去等絕弦。

translations.literal: Flowered axles raise dust—coming like a swift arrow; sparrow net briefly set—going like a broken string.
translations.idiomatic: Gilded wheels raise dust as they arrive like a flying arrow; the sparrow net is hung for a moment, then they are gone as though a string had snapped.

sentences.zh: 飴蜜非甘，山川未阻，千變萬化，鬼出神入。

translations.literal: Sweet honey is not sweet, mountains and rivers do not obstruct—thousands of changes, ghost exits spirit enters.
translations.idiomatic: No sweetness binds them, no distance holds them back; they shift by the thousand, appearing and vanishing like spirits.

sentences.zh: 為此者皆衣冠士族，或有藝能，不恥不仁，不畏不義，靡愧友朋，莫慚妻子。

translations.literal: All who do this are gentry clans, some with talent—unashamed of lacking benevolence, unafraid of lacking righteousness, not ashamed before friends, not blushful before wives.
translations.idiomatic: Those who behave thus are men of pedigree, some even gifted—yet they feel no shame at lacking benevolence or righteousness, and neither friends nor wives can make them blush.

sentences.zh: 外呈厚貌，內蘊百心，繇是則紆青佩紫，牧州典郡，冠幘劫人，厚自封殖。

translations.literal: Outwardly thick countenance, inwardly a hundred hearts—thereby they wear purple and green, govern states and hold prefectures, caps and kerchiefs rob people, thickly enrich themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly respectable, inwardly treacherous, they win purple robes and green sashes, rule provinces and prefectures, and under official caps plunder and fatten themselves.

sentences.zh: 妍歌妙舞，列鼎撞鐘，耳倦絲桐，口飫珍旨。

translations.literal: Lovely songs and wonderful dances, arrayed cauldrons and striking bells—ears weary of silk strings, mouths sated with delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: They fill their halls with song and dance, cauldrons and bells, until their ears are weary of lute strings and their mouths are glutted with delicacies.

sentences.zh: 雖素論以為非，而時宰之不責，末俗蚩蚩，如此之敝。

translations.literal: Though plain discussion holds it wrong, the rulers of the time do not blame—final customs foolish and foolish, flaws such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Right-minded men condemn such conduct, yet the rulers of the day do not reprove it; the vulgar age wallows in evils like these.

sentences.zh: 余則違時薄宦，屏息窮居，甚恥驅馳，深畏乾沒。

translations.literal: I then opposed the times in slight office, held breath in poor dwelling, greatly shamed by hurrying to and fro, deeply feared grasping and seizing.
translations.idiomatic: I have gone against the age in a humble post, living quietly in seclusion, ashamed of the chase for office and deeply afraid of grasping gain.

sentences.zh: 心若死灰，不營勢利，家無儋石，不費囊錢。

translations.literal: Heart like dead ash, not scheming power and profit; home without a stone's excess, not spending purse money.
translations.idiomatic: My heart is like dead ash, untouched by power or profit; I keep no surplus at home and spend nothing from my purse.

sentences.zh: 偶影聯官，將數十載，駑拙致笑，輕生所以告勞也。

translations.literal: By chance shadow linked with office for nearly several decades—dull stupidity draws laughter; my light life is therefore told in toil.
translations.idiomatic: By chance I have held office for some decades, and my dullness has been laughed at—that is why I speak of the toils of a modest life.

sentences.zh: 真人禦宇，斫雕為樸，人知榮辱，時反邕熙。

translations.literal: The True Man holds the realm, carves ornament into plain—people know glory and shame, the age returns to harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Our sage sovereign rules the realm, stripping ornament back to simplicity, so that men again know honor from shame and the age returns to peace.

sentences.zh: 風力上宰，內敷文教，方、邵重臣，外揚武節。

translations.literal: Wind power—the chief minister within spreads culture and teaching; Fang and Shao—the great ministers without raise martial banners.
translations.idiomatic: Within, the chief minister spreads culture and learning; without, great ministers like Fang and Shao display martial authority.

sentences.zh: 被之大道，洽以淳風，舉必以才，爵無濫授。

translations.literal: Covered by the great Way, blended with pure wind—promotions always by talent, ranks without reckless granting.
translations.idiomatic: The great Way covers all, pure customs prevail, appointments go only to the capable, and ranks are never handed out lightly.

sentences.zh: 稟斯首鼠，不預衣簪，阿党比周，掃地俱盡，輕薄之儔，滅影竄跡。

translations.literal: Bearing this I am first like a rat, not joining robe and hairpin; flatterers banding together, swept clean altogether; light and frivolous sort, vanished traces in hiding.
translations.idiomatic: In such a time I have kept to the sidelines and never joined the gowned officials; cliques of flatterers have been swept away, and the frivolous have vanished without a trace.

sentences.zh: 礫石變成瑜瑾，莨莠化為芝蘭。

translations.literal: Gravel stones transform into gems, cocklebur becomes orchid and lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Pebbles are transformed into jade, and weeds into orchids and sacred fungus.

sentences.zh: 曩之扇俗攪時，駭耳穢目，今悉不聞不見，莫餘敢侮。

translations.literal: Formerly what stirred custom and time, shocked ear and fouled eye—now all unheard and unseen, none who dare slight me.
translations.idiomatic: What once shocked the ear and offended the eye no longer stirs the age; such things are neither heard nor seen, and none dares treat me with contempt.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：'聖人作而萬物睹'，斯之謂乎！」

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'When the sage arises, the myriad things behold'—is this not meant?'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "When the sage appears, all things look up to him"—is that not exactly this?"

sentences.zh: 歲餘，被征，奉詔郊勞陳使。

translations.literal: After a year more, he was summoned, received the decree to greet Chen envoys at the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was recalled and ordered to welcome the Chen envoys at the suburban ceremony.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遭母憂，未幾，起為散騎侍郎，奏內史侍郎事。

translations.literal: Before long he met with mother's mourning; soon after he was recalled as General of the Household for All-Purpose Attendants, presenting affairs of the Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his mother died; before long he was recalled as Attendant-in-Ordinary and reported on the duties of the Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 于時議置六卿，將除大理。

translations.literal: At that time discussion was held on establishing the Six Ministries—they were about to abolish the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court debated establishing the Six Ministries and was about to abolish the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 思道上奏曰：「省有駕部，寺留太僕，省有刑部，寺除大理，斯則重畜產而賤刑名，誠為未可。」

translations.literal: Sidao memorialized: 'The ministry has a Department of Carriages; the court retains the Imperial Stud—the ministry has a Department of Punishments; the court abolishes Judicial Review—this then values livestock and devalues penal names—truly it cannot be done.'
translations.idiomatic: Sidao submitted a memorial saying, "If the ministry keeps the Bureau of Carriages while the court retains the Imperial Stud, and the ministry has a Bureau of Punishments while the court abolishes the Court of Judicial Review, then livestock will be prized above the law—that truly will not do."

sentences.zh: 又陳殿庭非杖罰之所，朝臣犯笞罪，請以贖論，上悉嘉納之。

translations.literal: He also stated that the palace hall is not a place for staff punishment; when court officials commit bamboo-whipping crimes, he asked that redemption be used—the Emperor fully praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the palace was no place for corporal punishment and asked that court officials who merited beating be allowed to redeem the penalty instead; the emperor approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 是歲，卒于京師，時年五十二。

translations.literal: That year he died in the capital; he was fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in the capital, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，遣使弔祭焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly regretted it and sent envoys to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned him and sent envoys to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷，行于時。

translations.literal: There is a collection of thirty juan circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of writings of thirty fascicles that circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子赤松，大業中，官至河東長史。

translations.literal: His son Chisong, in the Daye reign period, reached office as administrator of Hedong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chisong, in the Daye era, rose to be administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 昌衡字子均。

translations.literal: Changheng, style name Zijun.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changheng, courtesy name Zijun.

sentences.zh: 父道虔，魏尚書僕射。

translations.literal: His father Daoxian was Wei Minister of Works Vice President.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoxian had been Vice Director of the Ministry of Works under Wei.

sentences.zh: 昌衡小字龍子，風神淡雅，容止可法，博涉經史，工草行書。

translations.literal: Changheng's childhood name was Longzi; spirit and bearing were elegant and light, deportment could serve as model; broadly mastered classics and histories, skilled in cursive and running script.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng's childhood name was Longzi. He was refined and composed, his bearing a model to others; he read widely in the classics and histories and excelled at cursive and running script.

sentences.zh: 從弟思道，小字釋奴，宗中俱稱英妙。

translations.literal: His cousin Sidao, childhood name Shinu—the clan together called both brilliant and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Sidao, childhood name Shinu, was with him acclaimed in the clan as the family's finest talents.

sentences.zh: 故幽州為之語曰：「盧家千里，釋奴、龍子。」

translations.literal: So Youzhou had a saying: 'A thousand li of the Lu family—Shinu and Longzi.'
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou therefore had a saying: "For a thousand li around, the Lu clan means Shinu and Longzi."

sentences.zh: 年十七，魏濟陰王元暉業召補太尉參軍事，兼外兵參軍。

translations.literal: At seventeen, Wei Prince of Jiyin Yuan Ye summoned him to fill Grand Minister of War attendant, concurrently External Troops attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he was summoned by Yuan Ye, Prince of Jiyin of Wei, and appointed attendant in the Grand Minister of War's office, with a concurrent post in external military affairs.

sentences.zh: 齊氏受禪，曆平恩令、太子舍人。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate, he successively held Ping'en magistrate, Crown Prince attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, he served successively as magistrate of Ping'en and attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 尋為僕射祖孝徵所薦，遷尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Soon recommended by Vice President Zuxiao, promoted to Department of Gold in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recommended by Vice Director Zuxiao and promoted to Director of the Gold Bureau in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 孝徵每曰：「吾用盧子均為尚書郎，自謂無愧幽州矣。」

translations.literal: Zuxiao often said: 'I used Lu Zijun as an officeholder in the Ministry—I deem myself not ashamed before Youzhou.'
translations.idiomatic: Zuxiao often said, "When I appointed Lu Zijun to the ministry, I felt I had done no disgrace to Youzhou."

sentences.zh: 其後兼散騎侍郎，迎勞周使。

translations.literal: Afterwards he also concurrently served as General Attendant Attendant, received and entertained Zhou envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also served concurrently as General Attendant and received envoys from Zhou.

sentences.zh: 武帝平齊，授司玉中士，與大宗伯斛斯徵修禮令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu pacified Qi, he was appointed Attendant of the Department of Jade in the Ministry of Rites, together with Grand Minister Hesixi revised ritual ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou conquered Qi, he was made Attendant of the Jade Bureau and, with Grand Minister Hesixi, revised the ritual codes.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜尚書祠部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Rites for Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites in charge of ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗大集群下，令自陳功績，人皆競進，昌衡獨無所言。

translations.literal: Gaozu once gathered the ministers below and ordered them to state their merits—everyone competed to advance; Changheng alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once assembled his ministers and ordered each to recount his achievements; everyone pressed forward except Changheng, who remained silent.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲目而異之。

translations.literal: Vice President Gao Feng looked at him with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Gao Feng regarded him with surprise.

sentences.zh: 陳使賀徹、周濆相繼來聘，朝廷每令昌衡接對之。

translations.literal: Chen envoys He Che and Zhou Fen successively came on embassy—the court each time ordered Changheng to receive them in audience.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen envoys He Che and Zhou Fen came on successive missions, the court each time assigned Changheng to receive them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為徐州總管長史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Before long, sent out as Administrator of the General Command of Xuzhou—very renowned for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as chief administrator under the Xuzhou commandery and won a strong reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書蘇威考之曰：「德為人表，行為士則。」

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Su Wei appraised him: 'Virtue is man's standard, conduct is the scholar's model.'
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Minister of Personnel, assessed him thus: "His virtue is the people's measure; his conduct is the scholar's pattern."

sentences.zh: 論者以為美談。

translations.literal: Discussants considered it fine talk.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators treated the remark as a celebrated saying.

sentences.zh: 嘗行至浚儀，所乘馬為他牛所觸，因致死。

translations.literal: Once traveling to Junyi, the horse he rode was touched by another's ox, and thus died.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while passing through Junyi, the horse he was riding was struck by another man's ox and killed.

sentences.zh: 牛主陳謝，求還價直，昌衡謂之曰：「六畜相觸，自關常理，此豈人情也，君何謝？」

translations.literal: The ox owner apologized and asked to return the price—Changheng said: 'The six domestic animals touching one another is itself ordinary principle—how is this human sentiment? Why do you apologize?'
translations.idiomatic: The ox's owner apologized and offered to pay compensation, but Changheng said, "When livestock collide it is only nature—what has that to do with human intent? Why apologize?"

sentences.zh: 拒而不受。

translations.literal: He refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and would take nothing.

sentences.zh: 性寬厚不校，皆此類也。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and did not carp—all were this kind.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was magnanimous and never quarreled; this was typical of him.

sentences.zh: 轉壽州總管長史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Administrator of the General Command of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator under the Shouzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 總管宇文述甚敬之，委以州務。

translations.literal: Commander Yuwen Shu greatly esteemed him and entrusted him with prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander Yuwen Shu greatly respected him and entrusted him with the prefecture's affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，遷金州刺史。

translations.literal: After a year more, promoted to Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was promoted to governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，奉詔持節為河南道巡省大使，及還，以奉使稱旨，授儀同三司，賜物三百段。

translations.literal: In the Renhou era, received decree holding insignia as Traveling Inspector of Henan Circuit; on return, for fulfilling the embassy mission he was granted Master of the Same Third Rank and bestowed three hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renhou period he was commissioned with imperial insignia as touring inspector of Henan; on his return, because his mission had pleased the throne, he was granted the rank of Master of the Same Third Order and three hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 昌衡自以年在懸車，表乞骸骨，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Changheng himself felt his years reached hanging-the-cart age, memorialized begging for bones—the generous edict did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng, feeling himself near seventy, submitted a memorial asking to retire, but a gracious edict refused permission.

sentences.zh: 大業初，征為太子左庶子，行詣洛陽，道卒，時年七十二。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, summoned as Left Attendant of the Heir Apparent; on the road going to Luoyang he died on the way—aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era he was summoned as Left Attendant of the Heir Apparent, but died on the road to Luoyang at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子寶素、寶胤。

translations.literal: Sons Baosu and Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Baosu and Baoyin.

sentences.zh: ○李孝貞

translations.literal: ○ Li Xiaozhen
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhen

sentences.zh: 李孝貞，字元操，趙郡柏人人也。

translations.literal: Li Xiaozhen, style Yuan'ao, was a man of Bo in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaozhen, courtesy name Yuancao, was a native of Bo in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父希禮，齊信州刺史，世為著姓。

translations.literal: His father Xili held the qi office of Xin's Inspector—the family for generations was a distinguished surname.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xili had been Inspector of Xin under Qi; the family had for generations been a prominent clan.

sentences.zh: 孝貞少好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: Xiaozhen from youth loved learning and could compose literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xiaozhen loved learning and could write well.

sentences.zh: 在齊釋褐司徒府參軍事。

translations.literal: Under Qi he donned the cloth cap as attendant in the Minister of Education's office.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi he entered service as an attendant in the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 簡靜不妄通賓客，與從兄儀曹郎中騷、太子舍人季節、博陵崔子武、范陽盧詢祖為斷金之契。

translations.literal: Quiet and restrained, not rashly receiving guests—with cousins Li Sao of the Personnel Bureau and Li Jijie, Crown Prince attendant, plus Cui Ziwu of Boling, Lu Xunzu of Fanyang—he formed bonds cut as metal.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and reserved, he did not casually receive guests; with his cousins Li Sao of the Personnel Bureau and Li Jijie, attendant to the crown prince, together with Cui Ziwu of Boling and Lu Xunzu of Fanyang, he formed friendships as firm as sworn brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 後以射策甲科拜給事中。

translations.literal: Later for archery examination top grade he was appointed Gentlemen Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, having placed first in the archery examination, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 于時黃門侍郎高乾和親要用事，求婚於孝貞。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director of the Yellow Gate Gao Qianhe was close kin and wielded power—he sought marriage with Xiaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Qianhe, Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, was a powerful favorite of the ruler and sought a marriage alliance with Xiaozhen.

sentences.zh: 孝貞拒之，由是有隙，陰譖之，出為太尉府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhen refused him; therefore there was a rift—secretly slandered him—sent out as external troops attendant in the Grand Minister's office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhen refused him; a breach followed, and Gao secretly slandered him until he was sent out as external troops attendant in the Grand Minister's office.

sentences.zh: 後曆中書舍人、博陵太守、司州別駕，複兼散騎常侍、聘周使副，還除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later successively Central Secretariat attendant, Boling Grand Administrator, Su Prefecture Vice Governor, again concurrently General Palace Attendant, deputy embassy to Zhou; on return appointed Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as attendant of the Central Secretariat, grand administrator of Boling, and vice governor of Su prefecture, then again as General Palace Attendant and deputy envoy to Zhou; on his return he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，授儀同三司、少典祀下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, appointed Master of the Same Third Rank, Lower Minister of Lesser Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he was granted the rank of Master of the Same Third Order and made Lower Minister of Lesser Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，轉吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, transferred to Lower Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Lower Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂相州，孝貞從韋孝寬擊之，以功授上儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Wei Cong rebelled at Xiangzhou—Xiaozhen followed Wei Xiaokuan in attacking him—for merit granted Senior Master of the Same Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chief minister, Wei Cong rebelled at Xiangzhou; Xiaozhen followed Wei Xiaokuan in the campaign and, for his merit, was granted Senior Master of the Same Third Order.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，拜馮翊太守，為犯廟諱，於是稱字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, appointed Grand Administrator of Fengyi—for violating temple taboo he therefore used his style name.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed grand administrator of Fengyi; because his name violated an imperial taboo, he thereafter used his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，遷蒙州刺史，吏民安之。

translations.literal: Several years later, promoted to Governor of Mengzhou—officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was promoted to governor of Mengzhou, where officials and people lived in peace under him.

sentences.zh: 自此不復留意於文筆，人問其故，慨然歎曰：「五十之年，倏焉而過，鬢垂素髮，筋力已衰，宦意文情，一時盡矣，悲夫！」

translations.literal: From this he no longer paid heed to brush and pen—when people asked the reason he sighed deeply: 'The year fifty—suddenly it passes; temples hang with white hair, sinews and strength already declined—official ambition and literary feeling in one moment all gone—alas!'
translations.idiomatic: From then on he no longer cared for writing; when people asked why, he sighed and said, "Fifty years pass in a blink; my temples are white and my strength is spent—office and letters are gone at once. How sad!"

sentences.zh: 然每暇日，輒引賓客弦歌對酒，終日為歡。

translations.literal: Yet on each idle day he would lead guests—sing with strings and wine facings—all day in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on his free days he would gather guests, sing to the lute, and drink with them, making merry all day long.

sentences.zh: 征拜內史侍郎，與內史李德林參典文翰。

translations.literal: Summoned as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, together with Vice Minister Li Delin jointly handled literary drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and, with Li Delin, shared responsibility for drafting state documents.

sentences.zh: 然孝貞無干劇之用，頗稱不理，上譴怒之，敕禦史劾其事，由是出為金州刺史。

translations.literal: Yet Xiaozhen had no use for urgent heavy affairs—many said he did not manage well—the Emperor reproved him in anger, ordered the censor to impeach the matter—thereby sent out as Governor of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xiaozhen proved unfit for demanding administrative work; many said he neglected his duties. The emperor rebuked him in anger and ordered the censor to investigate, whereupon he was sent out as governor of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still serving in office.

sentences.zh: 所著文集二十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: The collected writings he authored, twenty fascicles, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A twenty-fascicle collection of his writings circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 有子允玉。

translations.literal: He had a son Yunyu.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Yunyu.

sentences.zh: 孝貞弟孝威，亦有雅望，大業中，官至大理少卿。

translations.literal: Xiaozhen's younger brother Xiaowei also had elegant renown; in the Daye era, he reached the post of Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhen's younger brother Xiaowei likewise enjoyed a fine literary reputation and, during Emperor Yang's Daye reign, rose to serve as Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: ○薛道衡從弟孺

translations.literal: ○ Xue Daohheng; younger cousin Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Xue Daohheng. (His younger cousin Ru is treated later in the chapter.)

sentences.zh: 薛道衡，字玄卿，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Daohheng, style name Xuanqing, was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daohheng, courtesy name Xuanqing, came from Fenyin in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖聰，魏濟州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cong was Governor of Jizhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cong had served as Governor of Jizhou under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父孝通，常山太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiaotong was Governor of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaotong had been Governor of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 道衡六歲而孤，專精好學。

translations.literal: Daohheng was orphaned at six and devoted himself single-mindedly to study.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng lost his father at the age of six and threw himself into his studies with single-minded devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十三，講《左氏傳》，見子產相鄭之功，作《國僑贊》，頗有詞致，見者奇之。

translations.literal: At age thirteen, lecturing on the Zuo Commentary, he saw Zichan's achievement as minister of Zheng, composed an "Encomium on Guo Qiao," with considerable literary grace; those who saw it marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, while studying the Zuo Commentary, he read of Zichan's statesmanship in Zheng and wrote an "Encomium on Guo Qiao" of real literary polish; all who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 其後才名益著，齊司州牧、彭城王浟引為兵曹從事。

translations.literal: Thereafter his talent and fame grew ever more prominent; the Prince of Pengcheng, You, as Governor of Sizhou, summoned him as an attendant in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His literary reputation soon spread further, and the Prince of Pengcheng, You, governor of Sizhou, appointed him an aide in the military bureau.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射弘農楊遵彥，一代偉人，見而嗟賞。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan of Hongnong, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—a great man of the age—saw him and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan of Hongnong, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and a towering figure of his generation, met him and exclaimed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 授奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He received appointment as Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書隴西辛術與語，歎曰：「鄭公業不亡矣。」

translations.literal: Xin Shu of Longxi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, conversed with him and sighed, saying: "Lord Zheng's enterprise has not perished."
translations.idiomatic: Xin Shu of Longxi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, spoke with him and sighed, "The legacy of the Lord of Zheng lives on."

sentences.zh: 河東裴讞目之曰：「自鼎遷河朔，吾謂關西孔子罕值其人，今複遇薛君矣。」

translations.literal: Pei Yan of Hedong fixed his gaze on him and said: "Since the tripod moved to north of the River, I thought one rarely met a Confucius of the Pass West; now I have again encountered Lord Xue."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yan of Hedong looked him over and declared, "Since the royal house moved north of the Yellow River, I had thought a sage of the western passes a rarity indeed—yet here I meet Master Xue again."

sentences.zh: 武成作相，召為記室，及即位，累遷太尉府主簿。

translations.literal: When Wucheng served as Chancellor, he summoned him as Recorder; when he ascended the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Chief Clerk of the Grand Marshal's office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wucheng was still chancellor, he summoned Daohheng as his recorder; after Wucheng took the throne, Daohheng rose in due course to chief clerk of the Grand Marshal's office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，兼散騎常侍，接對周、陳二使。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was concurrently made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and received envoys from Zhou and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was also made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and charged with receiving envoys from Northern Zhou and Chen.

sentences.zh: 武平初，詔與諸儒修定《五禮》，除尚書左外兵郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping, an edict ordered him with various Confucians to revise and fix the Five Rites; he was appointed Left Outer Military Officer of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wuping era he was ordered, together with other scholars, to help revise the Five Rites, and was appointed Left Outer Military Officer in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 陳使傅縡聘齊，以道衡兼主客郎接對之。

translations.literal: Chen's envoy Fu Zuan came on a mission to Qi; Daohheng was made concurrent Chief of Guests to receive and answer him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen sent Fu Zuan on a mission to Qi, Daohheng was appointed concurrent Chief of Guests to receive him.

sentences.zh: 縡贈詩五十韻，道衡和之，南北稱美。

translations.literal: Zuan presented a poem of fifty rhymes; Daohheng replied in kind, and north and south alike praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zuan presented a fifty-rhyme poem, which Daohheng answered in matching verse; both north and south acclaimed the exchange.

sentences.zh: 魏收曰：「傅縡所謂以蚓投魚耳。」

translations.literal: Wei Shou said: "What Fu Zuan did was what they call casting a worm to a fish."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou remarked, "Fu Zuan was like a man baiting a fishhook with a worm—hopelessly outmatched."

sentences.zh: 待詔文林館，與范陽盧思道、安平李德林齊名友善。

translations.literal: He awaited imperial orders at the Wulin Pavilion and was equally famed and friendly with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Li Delin of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a literary attendant at the Wulin Pavilion and was ranked alongside Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Li Delin of Anping, with whom he was on close terms.

sentences.zh: 複以本官直中書省，尋拜中書侍郎，仍參太子侍讀。

translations.literal: Again with his original office he served duty at the Secretariat; soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and still participated as Reader Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He continued in his post while serving on duty at the Secretariat, and was soon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, remaining a reader-attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後主之時，漸見親用，于時頗有附會之譏。

translations.literal: In the time of the Last Ruler, he was gradually seen in intimate employment; at the time there was considerable criticism of currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Last Ruler he came increasingly into favor, though many at the time accused him of sycophancy.

sentences.zh: 後與侍中斛律孝卿參預政事，道衡具陳備周之策，孝卿不能用。

translations.literal: Later, together with Attendant-in-Chief Hulu Xiaoxiao, he participated in government affairs; Daohheng fully set forth a strategy for guarding against Zhou, which Xiaoxiao could not employ.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Attendant-in-Chief Hulu Xiaoxiao in deliberating state affairs and laid out a full plan for defending against Zhou, but Xiaoxiao would not adopt it.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，周武引為禦史二命士。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Emperor Wu of Zhou summoned him as a Second-Rank Gentleman of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Qi, Emperor Wu of Zhou appointed him Second-Rank Gentleman of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，自州主簿入為司祿上士。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his home district; from Provincial Chief Clerk he entered office as Senior Gentleman of the Bureau of Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned home and, after serving as a provincial chief clerk, entered the capital as Senior Gentleman of the Bureau of Revenues.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，從元帥梁睿擊王謙，攝陵州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu served as Chancellor, he followed the Commander-in-Chief Liang Rui in attacking Wang Qian and acted as Governor of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was chancellor, he followed the commander Liang Rui against Wang Qian and served as acting governor of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大定中，授儀同，攝邛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Dading era he was granted the title of Palace Attendant of the First Rank and acted as Governor of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dading era he was made Palace Attendant of the First Rank and served as acting governor of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，坐事除名。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, for an offense he was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Daohheng was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 河間王弘北征突厥，召典軍書，還除內史舍人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian, Hong, on the northern expedition against the Turks, summoned him to manage military documents; on return he was appointed Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hejian, Hong, marched north against the Turks, he summoned Daohheng to manage military correspondence; on his return Daohheng was appointed Secretary of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年，兼散騎常侍，聘陳主使。

translations.literal: That year, concurrently Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, he was envoy on a mission to the Lord of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was also made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and sent as envoy to the Chen court.

sentences.zh: 道衡因奏曰：「江東蕞爾一隅，僭擅遂久，實由永嘉已後，華夏分崩。

translations.literal: Daohheng thereupon memorialized, saying: "The lands east of the River are but a tiny corner, yet they have usurped rule for so long—truly because after the Yongjia era the Central Realm split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng then submitted a memorial: "The southeast is but a petty corner of the realm, yet it has long played at kingship—ever since the Yongjia reign, when the heartland fell apart.

sentences.zh: 劉、石、符、姚、慕容、赫連之輩，妄竊名號，尋亦滅亡。

translations.literal: The clans of Liu, Shi, Fu, Yao, Murong, Helian, and the like presumptuously stole titles and soon perished as well.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu, Shi, Fu, Yao, Murong, and Helian regimes all seized titles without right and were extinguished in their turn.

sentences.zh: 魏氏自北徂南，未遑遠略。

translations.literal: The Wei house moved from north to south and had no leisure for distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei moved southward they had no leisure to pursue distant conquests.

sentences.zh: 周、齊兩立，務在兼併，所以江表逋誅，積有年祀。

translations.literal: Zhou and Qi stood as two states, their effort set on mutual annexation—hence south of the River long evaded punishment, piling up years and seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Qi were locked in rivalry for supremacy, so the south escaped punishment year after year.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖德天挺，光膺寶祚，比靈斯三代，平一九州，豈容使區區之陳，久在天網之外？
