translations.literal: Your Majesty's sagely virtue is heaven-raised; you brightly received the precious throne, comparable in spirit to the Three Dynasties, unifying the Nine Provinces—how can one allow petty Chen to long remain outside the heavenly net?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's sacred virtue matches Heaven itself; you have taken the throne and may be compared with the sage kings of antiquity in unifying the realm—how can petty Chen be left outside the imperial net any longer?

sentences.zh: 臣今奉使，請責以稱籓。」

translations.literal: Your servant now on this mission asks to demand of them that they declare themselves a vassal state."
translations.idiomatic: On this mission I ask leave to demand that Chen acknowledge vassal status."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「朕且含養，置之度外，勿以言辭相折，識朕意焉。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "For now I will nourish and cherish them, set them beyond measure, do not use words to break them—understand my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "For now I mean to show forbearance and set them outside my immediate concern. Do not press them with harsh words; understand my intent."

sentences.zh: 江東雅好篇什，陳主尤愛雕蟲，道衡每有所作，南人無不吟誦焉。

translations.literal: The lands east of the River elegantly loved literary pieces; the Lord of Chen especially loved ornamental verse—whenever Daohheng produced something, southerners none failed to chant and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast had always prized poetry, and the Chen ruler was especially fond of ornamental verse; whatever Daohheng wrote was soon on everyone's lips south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 及八年伐陳，授淮南道行台尚書吏部郎，兼掌文翰。

translations.literal: When in the eighth year they attacked Chen, he was appointed Director of Personnel in the Secretariat of the Huainan Circuit Field Headquarters and concurrently managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Chen was launched in the eighth year, he was appointed Director of Personnel on the Huainan campaign staff and also took charge of official correspondence.

sentences.zh: 王師臨江，高熲夜坐幕下，謂之曰：「今段之舉，克定江東已不？

translations.literal: When the royal army reached the river, Gao Jiong sat under the tent at night and said to him: "This present undertaking—will it already subdue the lands east of the River?
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial army reached the Yangtze, Gao Jiong sat in his tent one night and asked him, "Will this campaign succeed in pacifying the southeast?

sentences.zh: 君試言之。」

translations.literal: My lord, try speaking on it."
translations.idiomatic: Give me your view."

sentences.zh: 道衡答曰：「凡論大事成敗，先須以至理斷之。

translations.literal: Daohheng answered: "Whenever one discusses success or failure in great affairs, one must first judge by supreme principle.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng replied, "In judging any great undertaking, one must first weigh it by the highest principles of right.

sentences.zh: 《禹貢》所載九州，本是王者封域。

translations.literal: The Nine Provinces recorded in the Tribute of Yu were originally the demesne of the true king.
translations.idiomatic: The nine provinces listed in the Tribute of Yu were originally the domain of the true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 後漢之季，群雄競起，孫權兄弟遂有吳、楚之地。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Han, competing heroes rose together; Sun Quan and his brothers then held the lands of Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Later Han, rival warlords sprang up, and Sun Quan and his brothers seized the Wu and Chu regions.

sentences.zh: 晉武受命，尋即吞併，永嘉南遷，重此分割。

translations.literal: When Jin Wu received the mandate, soon he swallowed and annexed; at the Yongjia southward migration, this partition was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne he soon reunified the realm, but the southward flight at Yongjia split the empire once again.

sentences.zh: 自爾已來，戰爭不息，否終斯泰，天道之恆。

translations.literal: From then until now, warfare has not ceased; when obstruction ends, peace follows—this is the constancy of Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Since then war has never ceased, yet when adversity reaches its limit, prosperity returns—such is the constant way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 郭璞有雲：'江東偏王三百年，還與中國合。

translations.literal: Guo Pu said: 'The partial kings east of the River for three hundred years will again unite with the Central States.'
translations.idiomatic: Guo Pu once prophesied, 'The separatist rulers of the southeast will hold sway for three hundred years, then reunite with the heartland.'

sentences.zh: '今數將滿矣。

translations.literal: Now the number is nearly full.
translations.idiomatic: That term is almost complete.

sentences.zh: 以運數而言，其必克一也。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of fate's reckoning, victory is certain—first point.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the turn of destiny, conquest is assured—that is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 有德者昌，無德者亡，自古興滅，皆由此道。

translations.literal: Those with virtue flourish; those without perish—from antiquity rise and fall have all followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: The virtuous prosper and the wicked perish; the rise and fall of states has always obeyed this law.

sentences.zh: 主上躬履恭儉，憂勞庶政，叔寶峻宇雕牆，酣酒荒色。

translations.literal: Our lord personally practices reverence and frugality, toiling over the myriad affairs of government; Shubao has lofty halls and carved walls, deep in wine and dissolute with women.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign is personally frugal and diligent in government, while Chen Shubao lives in palaces of carved splendor, drowning in wine and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 上下離心，人神同憤，其必克二也。

translations.literal: Above and below are estranged in heart; men and spirits alike rage—victory is certain, second point.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and subjects are divided, and both men and gods are incensed—that is the second assurance of victory.

sentences.zh: 為國之體，在於任寄，彼之公卿，備員而已。

translations.literal: The substance of governing a state lies in entrusting office; their dukes and ministers are mere placeholders.
translations.idiomatic: A state's strength lies in whom it appoints; Chen's ministers are mere figureheads.

sentences.zh: 拔小人施文慶委以政事，尚書令江總唯事詩酒，本非經略之才，蕭摩訶、任蠻奴是其大將，一夫之用耳。

translations.literal: They promoted the petty man Shi Wenqing and entrusted him with government affairs; Director of the Department Jiang Zong devotes himself only to poetry and wine—originally no talent for strategy; Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu are their great generals, fit for but one man's use.
translations.idiomatic: They have elevated the petty official Shi Wenqing to run the government, while Director Jiang Zong cares only for wine and verse and has no gift for strategy; their chief generals Xiao Mohe and Ren Mannu are worth no more than a single soldier each.

sentences.zh: 其必克三也。

translations.literal: Victory is certain, third point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third assurance of victory.

sentences.zh: 我有道而大，彼無德而小，量其甲士，不過十萬。

translations.literal: We have the Way and are great; they lack virtue and are small—estimating their armored soldiers, they do not exceed one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: We possess the Way and are mighty; they lack virtue and are weak—and their armed forces number no more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 西自巫峽，東至滄海，分之則勢懸而力弱，聚之則守此而失彼。

translations.literal: West from the Wu Gorges, east to the blue sea—if divided, their momentum hangs aloft and strength is weak; if gathered, they guard this and lose that.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wu Gorges in the west to the eastern sea, if their forces are divided their strength is feeble, and if massed together they cannot defend every point at once.

sentences.zh: 其必克四也。

translations.literal: Victory is certain, fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth assurance of victory.

sentences.zh: 席捲之勢，其在不疑。」

translations.literal: The momentum of rolling up a mat—there is no doubt in it."
translations.idiomatic: A sweeping victory is beyond doubt."

sentences.zh: 熲忻然曰：「君言成敗，事理分明，吾今豁然矣。

translations.literal: Jiong said with pleasure: "My lord's words on success and failure—the principle and facts are clear; I am now suddenly enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong said with delight, "Your analysis of victory and defeat is lucid in both principle and fact—I understand it perfectly now.

sentences.zh: 本以才學相期，不意籌略乃爾。」

translations.literal: I originally looked to you for talent and learning; I did not expect strategic planning to be thus."
translations.idiomatic: I had valued you for literary talent alone—I never expected such strategic insight."

sentences.zh: 還除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 後坐抽擢人物，有言其党蘇威，任人有意故者，除名，配防嶺表。

translations.literal: Later, for promoting persons in office, there were words that he factioned with Su Wei and appointed people with private motives; he was struck from the registers and assigned to guard the Lingnan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed for favoring certain appointees; critics said he sided with Su Wei and chose officials for private reasons, and he was stripped of rank and sent to serve on the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣時在揚州，陰令人諷道衡從揚州路，將奏留之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin, Guang, was then in Yangzhou; secretly he sent someone to hint to Daohheng to take the Yangzhou route, intending to memorialize to retain him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Guang, was then in Yangzhou and secretly had someone suggest that Daohheng travel by way of Yangzhou, planning to petition the throne to keep him there.

sentences.zh: 道衡不樂王府，用漢王諒之計，遂出江陵道而去。

translations.literal: Daohheng was not pleased with the princely mansion; using the Prince of Han Liang's plan, he then departed by the Jiangling route.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng had no wish to join a prince's household and, following a plan of the Prince of Han, Liang, took the Jiangling road instead.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔征還，直內史省。

translations.literal: Soon an edict summoned him back; he served duty at the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled by imperial order and resumed duty at the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 晉王由是銜之，然愛其才，猶頗見禮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin therefore harbored resentment toward him, yet loving his talent, still treated him with considerable courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin bore a grudge over this, yet still valued his talent and treated him with considerable respect.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，授內史侍郎，加上儀同三司。

translations.literal: Several years later, he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and additionally made Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and additionally granted the rank of Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 道衡每至構文，必隱坐空齋，蹋壁而臥，聞戶外有人便怒，其沉思如此。

translations.literal: Whenever Daohheng came to compose a text, he would seclude himself in an empty study, kick the wall and lie down; if he heard someone outside the door he grew angry—such was his deep thought.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Daohheng set out to write, he would shut himself in an empty room, lie against the wall, and fly into a rage if he heard anyone outside—so intensely did he concentrate.

sentences.zh: 高祖每曰：「薛道衡作文書稱我意。」

translations.literal: Gaozu often said: "Xue Daohheng's compositions of documents match my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often remarked, "Xue Daohheng's official writings always suit my meaning."

sentences.zh: 然誡之以迂誕。

translations.literal: Yet he admonished him for being roundabout and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also warned him against being ponderous and overwrought.

sentences.zh: 後高祖善其稱職，謂楊素、牛弘曰：「道衡老矣，驅使勤勞，宜使其硃門陳戟。」

translations.literal: Later Gaozu was pleased with his fulfilling his duties and said to Yang Su and Niu Hong: "Daohheng is old; driven in toil and labor—he should have halberds displayed at his vermilion gate."
translations.idiomatic: Later, pleased with his service, Gaozu told Yang Su and Niu Hong, "Daohheng is growing old yet still toils diligently for the court—it is time he had halberds set before his gate as a mark of honor."

sentences.zh: 於是進位上開府，賜物百段。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was advanced to Upper Defender of the Office and granted a hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly promoted to Upper Defender of the Office and rewarded with a hundred lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 道衡辭以無功，高祖曰：「爾久勞階陛，國家大事，皆爾宣行，豈非爾功也？」

translations.literal: Daohheng declined on the ground of no achievement; Gaozu said: "You have long toiled on the palace steps; the great affairs of state—all are proclaimed and carried out by you—is this not your achievement?"
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng protested that he had earned no such honor, but Gaozu said, "You have long labored at court, and the great affairs of state are all drafted and proclaimed through you—is that not achievement enough?"

sentences.zh: 道衡久當樞要，才名益顯，太子諸王爭相與交，高熲、楊素雅相推重，聲名籍甚，無競一時。

translations.literal: Daohheng long held crucial posts; talent and fame grew ever more prominent; the Heir Apparent and princes vied to associate with him; Gao Jiong and Yang Su in their plainness mutually esteemed him—his reputation was very great, without rival in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng had long held key posts at court, and his fame only grew; the crown prince and imperial princes competed for his friendship, while Gao Jiong and Yang Su held him in the highest regard. His reputation in that age had no equal.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，楊素專掌朝政，道衡既與素善，上不欲道衡久知機密，因出檢校襄州總管。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era, Yang Su alone controlled court government; Daohheng was already on good terms with Su—the Emperor did not wish Daohheng to long know secrets, and therefore sent him out to inspect and act as Administrator of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era Yang Su dominated the government; because Daohheng was close to him, the emperor did not want him privy to state secrets for too long and sent him out as acting administrator of Xiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 道衡久蒙驅策，一旦違離，不勝悲戀，言之哽咽。

translations.literal: Daohheng had long received the whip of service; in one day to part in violation—he could not bear grief and longing, and speaking of it his voice choked.
translations.idiomatic: Daohheng had served at court for many years, and the sudden parting overwhelmed him with grief; he could hardly speak for weeping.

sentences.zh: 高祖愴然改容曰：「爾光陰晚暮，侍奉誠勞。

translations.literal: Gaozu, mournful, changed his expression and said: "Your years' light is late dusk; in attendance you are truly toilsome.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's face fell with sorrow as he said, "You are in the evening of your years, and your service to me has been unstinting.

sentences.zh: 朕欲令爾將攝，兼撫萌俗。

translations.literal: I wish to have you take charge and oversee, and also comfort the budding folkways.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to have you govern there and nurture the people as well.

sentences.zh: 今爾之去，朕如斷一臂。」

translations.literal: Now that you go, I am as if one arm were cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Your departure feels to me like losing an arm."

sentences.zh: 於是賚物三百段，九環金帶，並時服一襲，馬十匹，慰勉遣之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed three hundred lengths of goods, a nine-ring gold belt, together with one suit of seasonal dress, and ten horses, comforted and exhorted him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him three hundred lengths of goods, a nine-ring gold belt, a suit of court dress, and ten horses, comforted him warmly, and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 在任清簡，吏民懷其惠。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and simple; officials and people cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In office he governed with simplicity and restraint, and officials and commoners alike cherished his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，轉番州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Governor of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Daohheng was transferred to governor of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，上表求致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he petitioned to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 帝謂內史侍郎虞世基曰：「道衡將至，當以秘書監待之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yu Shiji: "Daohheng is about to arrive; he should be received as Director of the Secretariat Library."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Vice Director Yu Shiji, "When Daohheng arrives, I shall appoint him Director of the Imperial Library."

sentences.zh: 道衡既至，上《高祖文皇帝頌》，其詞曰：

translations.literal: When Daohheng had arrived, he presented an "Eulogy for Emperor Wen, the Literary Emperor, the High Ancestor"; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: When Daohheng arrived, he presented his "Eulogy for Emperor Wen, the Literary High Ancestor." It begins:

sentences.zh: 太始太素，荒茫造化之初；

translations.literal: Great Beginning, Great Simplicity—the vast void at the dawn of creation;
translations.idiomatic: In the Great Beginning and Great Simplicity, at the vast dawn of creation—

sentences.zh: 天皇地皇，杳冥書契之外。

translations.literal: Heavenly Emperor, Earthly Emperor—obscure darkness beyond written contracts.
translations.idiomatic: the Heavenly and Earthly Sovereigns, in the dim reaches before any written record.

sentences.zh: 其道絕，其跡遠，言談所不詣，耳目所不追。

translations.literal: Their Way is cut off, their traces far—speech and talk do not reach them, ear and eye do not pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: Their way is beyond reach and their traces remote—beyond the reach of words, beyond what eye or ear can follow.

sentences.zh: 至於入穴登巢，鶉居鷇飲，不殊於羽族，取類于毛群，亦何貴於人靈，何用於心識？

translations.literal: As for entering caves and climbing nests, quail dwelling and nestling to drink—not different from winged tribes, taking kind with hairy herds—what then is precious in human spirit, what use in mind and knowing?
translations.idiomatic: When men lived in caves and nests, dwelling like quail and drinking like nestlings, they differed little from birds and beasts—what then made the human spirit precious, or reason of any use?

sentences.zh: 羲、軒已降，爰暨唐、虞，則乾象而施法度，觀人文而化天下，然後帝王之位可重，聖哲之道為尊。

translations.literal: From Xi and Xuan downward, reaching to Tang and Yu—then they modeled the heavenly signs and instituted laws and measures, observed human patterns and transformed all under Heaven; only then could the throne of emperor and king be honored, the Way of sage and wise be revered.
translations.idiomatic: From Fu Xi and the Yellow Emperor down to Yao and Shun, rulers modeled themselves on Heaven, established laws, and cultivated civilization—only then did the throne gain its dignity and the sage's Way its authority.

sentences.zh: 夏後、殷、周之國，禹、湯、文、武之主，功濟生民，聲流《雅頌》，然陵替於三五，慚德於干戈。

translations.literal: The states of Xia, Yin, and Zhou—the lords Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—merit aiding the living people, fame flowing in the Odes and Hymns; yet they declined in the Three and Five, ashamed in virtue before arms and halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasties of Xia, Shang, and Zhou, and rulers such as Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, brought benefit to the people and won praise in the Book of Odes—yet even they declined in the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors era, their virtue shamed by ceaseless war.

sentences.zh: 秦居閏位，任刑名為政本，漢執靈圖，雜霸道而為業。

translations.literal: Qin occupied the intercalary position, taking punishments and names as the root of government; Han grasped the numinous chart, mixing hegemonic ways as their enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Qin seized power between dynasties and made legalist punishment the foundation of rule; Han held the Mandate yet mingled hegemonic methods with true kingship.

sentences.zh: 當塗興而三方峙，典午末而四海亂。

translations.literal: When the Tujia line rose, three sides stood opposed; at the end of the Dian-Wu era, the four seas were in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei rose, three kingdoms confronted one another; by the end of the Jin, the empire was torn by chaos.

sentences.zh: 九州封域，窟穴鯨鯢之群；

translations.literal: The Nine Provinces' bounded lands—cave-dwelling schools of whales and crocodiles;
translations.idiomatic: Within the nine provinces, monsters and rebels lurked in their lairs;

sentences.zh: 五都遺黎，蹴踏戎馬之足。

translations.literal: The remnant people of the five capitals—trampled under the hooves of war-horses.
translations.idiomatic: the surviving peoples of the great cities trampled beneath the hooves of war.

sentences.zh: 雖玄行定嵩、洛，木運據崤、函，未正滄海之流，詎息昆山之燎！

translations.literal: Although the dark line fixed Song and Luo, the wood fate held Xiao and Han—they did not rectify the flow of the blue sea; how could they extinguish the blaze on Kunshan!
translations.idiomatic: Though the Northern Wei settled Song and Luoyang and the Liang held the passes of Xiao and Han, none could set the eastern sea in order or quench the fires of civil war!

sentences.zh: 協千齡之旦暮，當萬葉之一朝者，其在大隋乎？

translations.literal: To harmonize the dawn and dusk of a thousand ages, to meet the morning of ten thousand leaves in one court— is it not in Great Sui?
translations.idiomatic: To gather the turning of a thousand years into a single dawn, to unite ten thousand generations in one reign—is this not the destiny of Great Sui?

sentences.zh: 粵若高祖文皇帝，誕聖降靈，則赤光照室，韜神晦跡，則紫氣騰天。

translations.literal: Thus was Gaozu, the Cultured Emperor: when the sage was born and the spirit descended, crimson light filled the chamber; when he hid his divinity and concealed his traces, purple vapor rose to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Gaozu, the Cultured Emperor: at his birth heaven sent a sage, and crimson light flooded the room; when he kept his powers hidden, purple mist climbed the sky.

sentences.zh: 龍顏日角之奇，玉理珠衡之異，著在圖籙，彰乎儀錶。

translations.literal: The marvel of a dragon countenance and sun-cornered brow, the strangeness of jade-lined forehead and pearl-set brow ridge, were recorded in charts and registers and made manifest in his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His dragon-like face and sun-cornered brow, the jade lines of his forehead and pearl-like ridges—marvels set down in prophecy and plain to see in his person.

sentences.zh: 而帝系靈長，神基崇峻，類邠、岐之累德，異豐、沛之勃起。

translations.literal: His imperial line was spiritually enduring, his divine foundation lofty and steep; it resembled the accumulated virtue of Bin and Qi, yet differed from the sudden rise of Feng and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: His house was long in sacred favor, its foundation towering—like the layered virtue of the Zhou at Bin and Qi, not like the abrupt ascent from Feng and Pei.

sentences.zh: 俯膺曆試，納揆賓門，位長六卿，望高百辟，猶重華之為太尉，若文命之任司空。

translations.literal: He bowed to accept the trials of the calendar, received the regency at the guest gate, stood first among the six ministers, and towered above the hundred lords—like Chonghua as Grand Marshal, like Wenming in charge as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He humbly underwent heaven's trials, took up governance at the court gate, headed the six ministers, and outshone every lord—like Shun as Grand Marshal, like Yu as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 蒼曆將盡，率土糜沸，玉弩驚天，金芒照野。

translations.literal: The azure mandate was nearing its end; all under heaven seethed like porridge; the jade crossbow startled the sky; golden rays lit the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The old mandate was failing; the realm boiled with strife; omens flashed in heaven and golden light swept the fields.

sentences.zh: 奸雄挺禍，據河朔而連海岱；

translations.literal: Traitors and strongmen raised calamity, holding the north of the Yellow River and linking to Mount Tai and the eastern sea;
translations.idiomatic: Villainous warlords rose in rebellion, holding the north country from the river to the eastern sea;

sentences.zh: 猾長縱惡，杜白馬而塞成皋。

translations.literal: Crafty chieftains unleashed wickedness, blocking White Horse and sealing Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: Cunning leaders ran riot, shutting the crossings at White Horse and Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 庸、蜀逆命，憑銅梁之險；

translations.literal: Yong and Shu defied the command, relying on the peril of Copper Beam;
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Shu defied the throne, trusting in the narrows of Copper Beam;

sentences.zh: 鄖、黃背誕，引金陵之寇。

translations.literal: Yun and Huang turned disloyal, drawing in raiders from Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: The Yun and Huang regions rebelled, beckoning invaders from Jinling.

sentences.zh: 三川已震，九鼎將飛。

translations.literal: The Three Rivers already quaked; the Nine Cauldrons were about to fly away.
translations.idiomatic: The heartland trembled; the imperial cauldrons seemed ready to pass from hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 高祖龍躍鳳翔，濡足授手，應赤伏之符，受玄狐之籙，命百下百勝之將，動九天九地之師，平共工而殄蚩尤，翦犬契窳而戮鑿齒。

translations.literal: Gaozu leaped like a dragon and soared like a phoenix, waded through water and lent his hand, answered the Red Submerged tally, received the Black Fox register, appointed generals victorious in a hundred descents, and moved armies of the nine heavens and nine earths; he pacified Gonggong and extinguished Chiyou, cut down Quanrong and slew Zaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rose like dragon and phoenix, plunged through flood and battle, fulfilled the Red Submerged prophecy and took heaven's mandate, set a hundred ever-victorious commanders in the field and roused hosts from every quarter—quelling rebels as ancient kings had quelled Gonggong and Chiyou, cutting down barbarian foes root and branch.

sentences.zh: 不煩二十八將，無假五十二征，曾未逾時，妖逆鹹殄，廓氛霧于區宇，出黎元於塗炭。

translations.literal: He did not trouble the twenty-eight generals, nor need the fifty-two campaigns; before the season had turned, rebels were all destroyed; he cleared mist from the realm and lifted the black-haired people from the mire and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: Without needing Han's twenty-eight generals or Zhou's fifty-two expeditions, he ended the revolt almost at once, cleared the land of turmoil, and rescued the people from ruin.

sentences.zh: 天柱傾而還正，地維絕而更紐。

translations.literal: The pillar of heaven, though tilted, was set upright again; the cords of earth, though broken, were tied anew.
translations.idiomatic: He righted the tilted pillar of heaven and retied the broken cords of earth.

sentences.zh: 殊方稽顙，識牛馬之內向；

translations.literal: Distant regions bowed their foreheads, knowing that cattle and horses turned inward;
translations.idiomatic: Far lands bowed low, knowing their herds and horses belonged once more to the center;

sentences.zh: 樂師伏地，懼鐘石之變聲。

translations.literal: Music masters prostrated themselves, fearing that bells and stones would change their tones.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians prostrated themselves, dreading that bells and chimes might never sound the old harmonies again.

sentences.zh: 萬姓所以樂推，三靈於是改卜。

translations.literal: Therefore the myriad people gladly pushed him forward, and the three spirits thereupon changed their divinations.
translations.idiomatic: The people gladly pressed him to rule; heaven, earth, and the spirits cast their lots anew in his favor.

sentences.zh: 壇場已備，猶弘五讓之心；

translations.literal: Though the altar and ritual ground were ready, he still upheld the heart of fivefold refusal;
translations.idiomatic: Though the altar stood ready, he still held to the fivefold refusal of the throne;

sentences.zh: 億兆難違，方從四海之請。

translations.literal: The hundred millions could not be gainsaid, and only then did he follow the petition of the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the myriad hosts could not be refused did he yield to the plea of all within the four seas.

sentences.zh: 光臨寶祚，展禮郊丘，舞六代而降天神，陳四圭而饗上帝，乾坤交泰，品物鹹亨。

translations.literal: He ascended to the precious throne, performed rites at the suburban mound, danced the six dynasties' dances to bring down the heavenly spirit, set out the four jades to feast the Supreme Lord; heaven and earth joined in peace, and all things alike prospered.
translations.idiomatic: He took the throne, offered rites at the suburban altar, danced the ancient sixfold rites to summon heaven, laid out the four jades to feast the Lord on High—and heaven and earth met in harmony, and every thing under them flourished.

sentences.zh: 酌前王之令典，改易徽號；

translations.literal: He drew on the worthy statutes of former kings and changed the imperial designation;
translations.idiomatic: He weighed the good ordinances of earlier kings and changed the dynastic name;

sentences.zh: 因庶萌之子來，移創都邑。

translations.literal: Because the sons of the common sprouts came to him, he moved and founded a new capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people came to him from every quarter, he moved the capital and built anew.

sentences.zh: 天文上當硃鳥，地理下據黑龍，正位辨方，揆影於日月，內宮外座，取法於辰象。

translations.literal: In celestial configuration it matched the Vermilion Bird above; in terrestrial form it rested on the Black Dragon below; he set positions and distinguished directions, measured shadows by sun and moon, and for inner palace and outer halls took his model from the starry signs.
translations.idiomatic: He aligned the capital with the Vermilion Bird in heaven and the Black Dragon on earth, set every quarter in its place by the sun and moon, and patterned inner palace and outer court on the stars.

sentences.zh: 懸政教于魏闕，朝群後於明堂，除舊佈新，移風易俗。

translations.literal: He displayed government and teaching at the Wei Gate tower, assembled the host of lords in the Bright Hall, removed the old and spread the new, and shifted customs and changed habits.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed his rule from the imperial gate, gathered the lords in the Bright Hall, swept away the old and set up the new, and transformed the manners of the age.

sentences.zh: 天街之表，地脈之外，獯獫孔熾，其來自久，橫行十萬，樊噲於是失辭，提步五千，李陵所以陷沒。

translations.literal: Beyond the Heavenly Street and outside the earth's veins, the Xianyun had long burned fierce; a hundred thousand rampaged, and even Fan Kuai was left speechless; five thousand on the march—thus Li Ling was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the frontier, the northern tribes had raged for ages; when a hundred thousand swept the border even Fan Kuai could find no answer, and five thousand men on the march were swallowed as Li Ling's army had been.

sentences.zh: 周、齊兩盛，競結旄頭，娉狄後於漠北，未足息其侵擾，傾珍藏于山東，不能止其貪暴。

translations.literal: In the two flourishing ages of Zhou and Qi they vied to win the barbarian chieftainess north of the desert, yet could not still the raids; they poured out treasures east of the mountains, yet could not halt their greed and violence.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zhou and Qi at their height courted barbarian queens beyond the desert and could not end the raids, poured out treasure from Shandong and could not satisfy their greed.

sentences.zh: 炎靈啟祚，聖皇馭宇，運天策於帷扆，播神威于沙朔，柳室、氈裘之長，皆為臣隸，瀚海、蹛林之地，盡充池苑。

translations.literal: When the Fiery Spirit opened its reign, the sage emperor ruled the realm; he wielded heaven's stratagems from behind the curtain, spread divine might over the sandy north; chiefs of felt tents and fur coats all became his servants, and the lands of the vast sea and the fenced forests all filled his parks.
translations.idiomatic: When Han's fiery mandate rose, the sage emperor held the realm: he plotted from the throne room and sent his might across the northern sands; chiefs of yurt and fur became his subjects, and steppe and forest became his hunting parks.

sentences.zh: 三吳、百越，九江五湖，地分南北，天隔內外，談黃旗紫蓋之氣，恃龍蟠獸據之險，恆有僭偽之君，妄竊帝王之號。

translations.literal: In the Three Wus, the Hundred Yue, the Nine Rivers and Five Lakes, land was split north and south and heaven divided inner from outer; they spoke of yellow banners and purple canopies, relied on dragon-coiled, beast-held strongholds, and constantly had usurping false kings who rashly stole the title of emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Yue, and the lands of the great rivers and lakes, north and south were sundered; men boasted of imperial omens and trusted in mountain fastnesses, and usurpers again and again seized the name of emperor.

sentences.zh: 時經五代，年移三百，爰降皇情，永懷大道，湣彼黎獻，獨為匪人。

translations.literal: Time passed through five dynasties and three hundred years shifted; then imperial feeling descended, ever cherishing the Great Way, pitying those black-haired offerings who alone were not true men.
translations.idiomatic: Five dynasties and three hundred years went by; then heaven's mercy descended, ever mindful of the Way, grieving that the people alone were left outside the human order.

sentences.zh: 今上利建在唐，則哲居代，地憑宸極，天縱神武，受脤出車，一舉平定。

translations.literal: The present sovereign, established in Tang, dwelt in wisdom at Dai; the earth supported him at the polar pivot, heaven gave free rein to his divine martial power; he received the sacrificial flesh and marched forth, and in one stroke brought peace.
translations.idiomatic: The present emperor, raised at Tang and wise in Dai, stood on the pivot of the realm with heaven-given martial genius; he took the war sacrifice and rode out, and in a single campaign brought all to order.

sentences.zh: 於是八荒無外，九服大同，四海為家，萬里為宅。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eight wilds had nothing outside them, the nine domains shared one great unity, the four seas became a single household, and ten thousand li became one dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Then nothing lay beyond the realm, the nine provinces were one, the four seas were a single home, and ten thousand li were one domain.

sentences.zh: 乃休牛散馬，偃武修文。

translations.literal: Then he rested the oxen and released the horses, laid down arms and cultivated culture.
translations.idiomatic: Then he put the oxen to pasture and freed the horses, sheathed the sword and turned to civil rule.

sentences.zh: 自華夏亂離，綿積年代，人造戰爭之具，家習澆偽之風，聖人之遺訓莫存，先王之舊典鹹墜。

translations.literal: Since Hua and Xia fell into disorder and separation, years piled up for long ages; men fashioned tools of war, and every household learned the ways of shallow falsity; the sage's bequeathed teaching did not remain, and the former kings' old statutes all fell away.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the heartland split in long disorder, generation after generation forged weapons of war and every house learned deceit; the sages' teaching was lost and the ancient kings' rites lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 爰命秩宗，刊定《五禮》，申敕太子，改正六樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he charged the Minister of Rites to revise and fix the Five Rites, and admonished the crown prince to correct the six kinds of music.
translations.idiomatic: He charged the Minister of Rites to compile the Five Rites and instructed the crown prince to restore the six classical modes.

sentences.zh: 玉帛樽俎之儀，節文乃備；

translations.literal: The rites of jade, silk, goblets, and stands were complete in their gradations and forms;
translations.idiomatic: The rites of jade, silk, and sacrificial vessels were complete in every detail;

sentences.zh: 金石匏革之奏，雅俗始分。

translations.literal: Performances of metal, stone, gourd, and hide were made, and refined and common music were first distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Music of bell, stone, pipe, and drum was ordered, and courtly and popular styles were set apart.

sentences.zh: 而留心政術，垂神聽覽，早朝晏罷，廢寢忘食，憂百姓之未安，懼一物之失所。

translations.literal: Moreover he fixed his mind on the arts of government, bent his spirit to listening and reviewing; he held early court and ended late, abandoned sleep and forgot to eat, fretted that the hundred surnames were not yet at peace, and feared that a single thing might be out of place.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his heart to governance, bent his attention to every petition, rose early and retired late, slept little and ate sparingly, anxious until the people were secure and fearful lest even one thing go wrong.

sentences.zh: 行先王之道，夜思待旦；

translations.literal: He walked the way of the former kings, thinking at night until dawn;
translations.idiomatic: He walked in the way of the ancient kings, pondering through the night until daybreak;

sentences.zh: 革百王之弊，朝不及夕。

translations.literal: He reformed the abuses of a hundred kings, with morning not reaching evening.
translations.idiomatic: He reformed the failings of a hundred reigns, reforming today what had been wrong yesterday.

sentences.zh: 見一善事，喜彰于容旨；

translations.literal: When he saw a single good deed, joy showed in his countenance;
translations.idiomatic: At the least good deed his face brightened with pleasure;

sentences.zh: 聞一愆犯，歎深於在予。

translations.literal: When he heard of a single fault or offense, he sighed deeply that the blame lay in himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the least offense he sighed that the fault was his own.

sentences.zh: 薄賦輕徭，務農重穀，倉廩有紅腐之積，黎萌無阻饑之慮。

translations.literal: He lightened taxes and eased corvée, devoted effort to agriculture and valued grain; the granaries held stores rotting red with surplus, and the black-haired sprouts had no fear of hunger blocking their way.
translations.idiomatic: He cut taxes and lightened labor service, put agriculture first and treasured grain; the granaries overflowed until grain spoiled, and the people no longer feared famine.

sentences.zh: 天性弘慈，聖心惻隱，恩加禽獸，胎卵於是獲全，仁沾草木，牛羊所以勿踐。

translations.literal: By nature he was vastly merciful, in sage heart compassionate; his grace reached birds and beasts, and embryos and eggs were thereby preserved; his benevolence touched grass and trees, and cattle and sheep were therefore not trampled.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was vast in mercy, his heart tender toward all; his kindness spared even beasts in the egg and womb, his benevolence reached grass and trees, and cattle and sheep went unharmed.

sentences.zh: 至於憲章重典，刑名大辟，申法而屈情，決斷於俄頃，故能彝倫攸敘，上下齊肅。

translations.literal: As for statutes and weighty codes, penal names and capital punishments, he upheld the law and bent private feeling, deciding in an instant—thus the constant relations were set in order and high and low alike were sternly disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In law and capital punishment he upheld the code over private feeling and judged in an instant, so that human relations were ordered and court and people alike stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 左右絕諂諛之路，縉紳無勢力之門。

translations.literal: At his left and right the road of flattery was cut off; among girdled sashes there was no gate of factional power.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery found no path to his side; the great families could buy no favor at court.

sentences.zh: 小心翼翼，敬事於天地；

translations.literal: Cautious and cautious, he reverently served heaven and earth;
translations.idiomatic: With utmost care he served heaven and earth;

sentences.zh: 終日乾乾，誡慎於亢極。

translations.literal: All day long diligent and striving, he was wary at the height of excess.
translations.idiomatic: All day he strove without slackening, ever watchful at the peak of power.

sentences.zh: 陶黎萌於德化，致風俗于太康，公卿庶尹，遐邇嶽牧，僉以天平地成，千載之嘉會，登封降禪，百王之盛典，宜其金泥玉檢，展禮介丘，飛聲騰實，常為稱首。

translations.literal: He molded the black-haired sprouts through moral transformation and brought customs to great peace; dukes, ministers, common administrators, lords near and far, and border shepherds all agreed that heaven was level and earth secure—a auspicious meeting of a thousand years; the feng and shan sacrifices, the grand ceremony of a hundred kings, were fitting for gold-sealed, jade-cased rites on Mount Jie, fame flying and merit rising—always to be named first.
translations.idiomatic: He shaped the people through virtue until the age knew great peace; every minister and border lord agreed that heaven and earth were in harmony—a moment that comes once in a thousand years. The feng and shan on Mount Tai, the supreme rite of a hundred kings, with seals of gold and cases of jade, were his by right; his fame and deeds should have led all others.

sentences.zh: 天子為而不恃，成而不居，沖旨凝邈，固辭弗許。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven acted yet did not rely on it, accomplished yet did not dwell on it; his modest purpose was deep and remote, and he firmly refused and would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: He acted yet claimed no credit, achieved yet would not rest in glory; his humble purpose ran deep, and he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 而雖休勿休，上德不德，更乃潔誠岱岳，遜謝愆咎。

translations.literal: Yet though he might have rested he did not rest; the highest virtue is not called virtue; further he purified his sincerity at Mount Dai and humbly declined, apologizing for faults.
translations.idiomatic: Though he might have ceased labor he did not; the highest virtue claims no virtue. Instead he purified himself at Mount Tai and humbly confessed his faults.

sentences.zh: 方知六十四卦，謙捴之道為尊，七十二君，告成之義為小，巍巍蕩蕩，無得以稱焉。

translations.literal: Then one knew that among the sixty-four hexagrams the way of modest yielding was honored, and that for the seventy-two rulers the meaning of announcing accomplishment was small—so lofty, so vast, that nothing could suffice to name it.
translations.idiomatic: Then men saw that among the sixty-four hexagrams humility was supreme, and that for the seventy-two kings who performed the feng sacrifice such announcement was a small thing—so towering and boundless that no words could measure him.

sentences.zh: 而深誠至德，感達於穹壤，和氣薰風，充溢於宇宙。

translations.literal: His deep sincerity and utmost virtue moved through dome and soil; harmonious qi and fragrant winds filled and overflowed the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: His deepest sincerity and highest virtue touched heaven and earth; harmonious breath and gentle winds filled the universe.

sentences.zh: 二儀降福，百靈薦祉，日月星象，風雲草樹之祥，山川玉石，鱗介羽毛之瑞，歲見月彰，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: The two principles sent down blessings; the hundred spirits presented felicity; omens in sun, moon, stars, and constellations, in wind, clouds, grass, and trees; auspicious signs in mountains, rivers, jade, and stone, in scaled, shelled, and feathered creatures—seen year by year, manifest month by month, beyond full reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth showered blessings; the hundred spirits offered good omens—in sun and moon, stars and sky, wind and cloud, grass and tree; in mountains, rivers, jade and stone, in every scaled and feathered creature. Year after year, month after month, they appeared beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 至於振古所未有，圖籍所不載，目所不見，耳所未聞。

translations.literal: As for things stirring the ages never before known, not recorded in charts and registers, never seen by the eye, never heard by the ear—
translations.idiomatic: Things never known since antiquity, unrecorded in any book, unseen by any eye, unheard by any ear—

sentences.zh: 古語稱聖人作，萬物睹，神靈滋，百寶用，此其效矣。

translations.literal: The old saying states: when the sage arises, the myriad things behold him; the spirits flourish, and the hundred treasures are employed—this was its effect.
translations.idiomatic: As the ancients said: when a sage appears, all things look to him, the spirits thrive, and every treasure finds its use—so it was with him.

sentences.zh: 既而游心姑射，脫屣之志已深；

translations.literal: Soon his mind wandered to Mount Guye, and the will to cast off his shoes ran deep;
translations.idiomatic: Soon his heart turned to the immortal peaks, and his wish to leave the world grew strong;

sentences.zh: 鑄鼎荊山，升天之駕遂遠。

translations.literal: He cast the cauldron at Mount Jing, and the carriage ascending to heaven passed far away.
translations.idiomatic: As Yu cast the cauldron at Mount Jing, his ascent to heaven carried him beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 凡在黎獻，具惟帝臣，慕深考妣，哀纏弓劍，塗山幽峻，無複玉帛之禮，長陵寂寞，空見衣冠之遊。

translations.literal: All among the black-haired offerings were wholly his imperial subjects; they yearned deeply for father and mother, grief wound round bow and sword; Mount Tu was dark and steep, and no more were the rites of jade and silk performed; Changling lay lonely, and only the wandering of robes and caps was seen.
translations.idiomatic: All the people were his subjects still; they mourned their lost father and mother, grief clinging to bow and sword. At Mount Tu no tribute came; at Changling only empty processions of court dress passed by.

sentences.zh: 若乃降精熛怒，飛名帝籙，開運握圖，創業垂統，聖德也；

translations.literal: As for descending essence and blazing glory, soaring name on the imperial register, opening fortune and grasping the chart, founding the enterprise and handing down the succession—this was sage virtue;
translations.idiomatic: His descent of sacred essence, his name inscribed in heaven's book, his opening of fortune and grasp of the mandate, his founding of the house and legacy for ages—this was sage virtue;

sentences.zh: 撥亂反正，濟國寧人，六合八紘，同文共軌，神功也；

translations.literal: Setting chaos aright and returning to the correct, saving the state and settling the people, the six harmonies and eight cords sharing script and track—this was divine achievement;
translations.idiomatic: He quelled disorder and restored order, saved the realm and gave the people peace, united the six directions in one script and one measure—this was divine achievement;

sentences.zh: 玄酒陶匏，雲和孤竹，禋祀上帝，尊極配天，大孝也；

translations.literal: Dark wine in earthen bowls, Yunhe and Guzhu music, solemn sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, honoring the utmost and matching heaven—this was great filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: With dark wine in earthen vessels and ancient music he sacrificed to the Lord on High, honoring heaven as his partner—this was the greatest filial piety;

sentences.zh: 偃伯戢戈，正禮裁樂，納民壽域，驅俗福林，至政也。

translations.literal: He stilled the martial lord and stored the halberds, rectified rites and trimmed music, brought the people into the domain of longevity, and drove custom into the forest of blessing—this was ultimate government.
translations.idiomatic: He sheathed the sword and stilled the drums, set rites right and trimmed music, brought the people into a realm of long life and led custom into abundance—this was government at its height.

sentences.zh: 張四維而臨萬宇，侔三皇而並五帝，豈直錙銖周、漢，麼麽魏、晉而已。

translations.literal: He spread the four bonds and looked down on the myriad realms, matched the Three Sovereigns and stood beside the Five Emperors—how could he be measured only by scruples against Zhou and Han, or by the mere trifles of Wei and Jin?
translations.idiomatic: He held the four pillars of rule over all the world, equaled the Three Sovereigns and stood with the Five Emperors—far more than a mere notch above Zhou and Han, infinitely beyond the petty ages of Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 雖五行之舞，每陳於清廟，九德之歌，無絕於樂府，而玄功暢洽，不局於形器，懿業遠大，豈盡於揄揚。

translations.literal: Though the Dance of the Five Agents was presented each time in the Clear Temple, and the Song of Nine Virtues never ceased in the Music Office, his dark merit flowed through all and was not confined to forms and vessels; his excellent work was far and great—how could it be exhausted in praise?
translations.idiomatic: Though the Dance of the Five Agents was offered in the ancestral temple and the Song of Nine Virtues never left the music bureau, his subtle achievement could not be bound in ritual form, his glorious work was too vast for any eulogy to exhaust.

sentences.zh: 臣輕生多幸，命偶興運，趨事紫宸，驅馳丹陛，一辭天闕，奄隔鼎湖，空有攀龍之心，徒懷蓐蟻之意。

translations.literal: Your servant, lightly born yet greatly favored, by fate met this rising fortune; I hurried to affairs in the Purple Forbidden Hall and raced along the cinnabar steps—once I left the heavenly gate, suddenly I was parted from Dinghu Lake; in vain I have the heart to climb after the dragon, in vain I cherish the feeling of the mat ants.
translations.idiomatic: I, a humble man most fortunate, was born into this glorious age; I served at the purple court and hurried along the scarlet steps—yet one farewell at the heavenly gate, and suddenly the emperor was gone beyond Dinghu. I can only yearn to follow the ascending dragon, can only grieve like ants upon his bier.

sentences.zh: 庶憑毫翰，敢希贊述！

translations.literal: I hope by brush and ink to dare to aspire to praise and narration!
translations.idiomatic: With brush in hand I dare hope to offer this praise!

sentences.zh: 昔堙海之禽不增於大地，泣河之士非益於洪流，盡其心之所存，望其力之所及，輒緣斯義，不覺斐然。

translations.literal: Of old the bird that filled the sea did not enlarge the great earth, nor did the man who wept at the river increase the mighty flood; I exhaust what my heart holds and look to the reach of my strength; following this principle, I cannot help but compose at length.
translations.idiomatic: As the bird that tried to fill the sea could not enlarge the earth, nor the man who wept before the river swell the flood, I give all my heart allows and all my strength can reach; moved by this duty, I have written at length unawares.

sentences.zh: 乃作頌曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed the eulogy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he composed the eulogy:

sentences.zh: 悠哉邃古，邈矣季世，四海九州，萬王千帝。

translations.literal: How far off the deep antiquity, how remote the late age; the four seas and nine provinces, ten thousand kings and a thousand emperors.
translations.idiomatic: How distant deep antiquity, how remote the fallen age—the four seas, nine provinces, ten thousand kings and a thousand emperors.

sentences.zh: 三代之後，其道逾替，爰逮金行，不勝其弊。

translations.literal: After the Three Dynasties their Way grew ever more decayed; when it reached the Metal Phase it could not bear its abuses.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties the Way declined ever further; when the Jin came, the rot could no longer be borne.

sentences.zh: 戎狄猾夏，群凶縱慝，竊號淫名，十有餘國。

translations.literal: Barbarians of Rong and Di ravaged Xia; a host of villains unleashed wickedness, usurping titles and extravagant names—more than a dozen states.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians ravaged the heartland; villains ran wild, stealing imperial titles—more than a dozen kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 怙威逞暴，悖禮亂德，五嶽塵飛，三象霧塞。

translations.literal: Relying on might they flaunted violence, betrayed rites and disordered virtue; dust flew on the five sacred peaks, mist choked the three emblems.
translations.idiomatic: They trusted in force and trampled rites and virtue; dust rose on the five peaks, mist shrouded the three emblems of rule.

sentences.zh: 玄精啟曆，發跡幽方，併吞寇偽，獨擅雄強。

translations.literal: The dark essence opened the calendar; he rose from a remote region, swallowed rebels and pretenders, and alone held heroic strength.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's dark mandate opened a new age; from a distant land he rose, swallowed rebels and usurpers, and stood alone in power.

sentences.zh: 載祀二百，比祚前王，江湖尚阻，區域未康。

translations.literal: For two hundred years of sacrifice he matched the reigns of former kings, yet rivers and lakes were still blocked and the regions not yet at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred years of rule matched the great dynasties of old, yet rivers and lakes were still divided and the land not yet whole.

sentences.zh: 句吳閩越，河朔渭涘，九縣瓜分，三方鼎跱。

translations.literal: Gouwu, Min, and Yue; north of the river and the banks of the Wei—the nine districts were carved like melon, three regions stood tripod-like.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, Min, and Yue; the north country and the Wei shore—the nine provinces were split apart, three powers stood like tripods.

sentences.zh: 狙詐不息，干戈競起，東夏雖平，亂離瘼矣。

translations.literal: Cunning and deceit did not cease; spears and shields vied to rise; though eastern Xia was pacified, disorder and separation brought affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Deceit never ceased, arms clashed without end; though the east was pacified, the land still groaned under division.

sentences.zh: 五運葉期，千年肇旦，赫矣高祖，人靈攸贊。

translations.literal: The five cycles bore their season; at the dawn of a thousand years, resplendent was Gaozu, and men and spirits alike praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The five phases turned to their hour; at the dawn of a new millennium Gaozu rose in splendor, and men and spirits acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 聖德迥生，神謀獨斷，癉惡彰善，夷凶靜難。

translations.literal: Sage virtue was born afar; divine strategy decided alone; he punished evil and displayed good, leveled the vicious and stilled calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred virtue arose anew; his counsel was heaven's alone—he punished the wicked, honored the good, swept away foes and stilled disaster.

sentences.zh: 宗伯撰儀，太史練日，孤竹之管，雲和之瑟。

translations.literal: The Minister of Rites drafted the ritual; the Grand Astrologer selected the day; pipes of Guzhu, zithers of Yunhe.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Rites drew up the rites, the Grand Historian chose the day; Guzhu pipes and Yunhe zithers sounded.

sentences.zh: 展禮上玄，飛煙太一，珪璧朝會，山川望秩。

translations.literal: He displayed rites to the Supreme Mystery, sent up smoke to the Grand Unity; jades and disks at the court assembly, mountains and rivers honored in due rank.
translations.idiomatic: He offered rites to heaven, sent smoke to the Grand Unity; jades were presented at court, mountains and rivers received their due sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 占揆星景，移建邦畿，下憑赤壤，上葉紫微。

translations.literal: He divined by stars and measured shadows, moved and built the capital region; below he rested on red soil, above he matched the Purple Tenuity.
translations.idiomatic: He read the stars and moved the capital, rooted on the red earth below, aligned with the Purple Palace above.

sentences.zh: 布政衢室，懸法象魏，帝宅天府，固本崇威。

translations.literal: He spread government in the Crossroads Chamber, hung laws at the Symbol Tower; the emperor's dwelling was heaven's storehouse, strengthening the root and exalting majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He governed from the great hall, proclaimed law from the tower gate; the imperial city was heaven's treasury, firming the foundation and lifting his awe.

sentences.zh: 匈河瀚海，龍荒狼望，種落陸梁，時犯亭障。

translations.literal: From the Xiongnu River to the vast sea, Dragon Wilderness and Wolf Outlook, tribes rose unruly and often violated the border posts.
translations.idiomatic: From the northern rivers to the desert sea, across the frontier wastes, tribes rose in rebellion and raided the border posts.

sentences.zh: 皇威遠懾，帝德遐暢，稽顙歸誠，稱臣內向。

translations.literal: Imperial might awed from afar, imperial virtue flowed to distant reaches; they bowed their foreheads and returned in sincerity, calling themselves subjects and turning inward.
translations.idiomatic: His majesty awed the far lands, his virtue reached every frontier; they bowed low and came in loyalty, calling themselves his subjects.

sentences.zh: 吳越提封，鬥牛星象，積有年代，自稱君長。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue held their domains, under the Dipper and Ox constellations; for accumulated years they called themselves lords and chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue held their territories under southern stars; for generations they styled themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 大風未繳，長鯨漏網，授鉞天人，豁然清蕩。

translations.literal: The great wind was not yet bound, the long whale slipped the net; the axe was given to the heaven-man, and suddenly all was cleared and swept clean.
translations.idiomatic: The storm had not yet been stilled, the great whale still escaped the net—then the commander of heaven received the axe, and all was suddenly swept clear.

sentences.zh: 戴日戴鬥，太平太蒙，禮教周被，書軌大同。

translations.literal: Bearing sun and bearing Dipper, great peace and vast obscurity; ritual teaching spread on every side, script and track were one in great unity.
translations.idiomatic: Under sun and stars, in vast peace, ritual reached every corner; writing and law were one throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 複禹之跡，成舜之功，禮以安上，樂以移風。

translations.literal: He restored Yu's footsteps and completed Shun's achievement; rites to settle those above, music to shift the winds of custom.
translations.idiomatic: He retraced Yu's path and fulfilled Shun's work—rites to secure the throne, music to transform the people.

sentences.zh: 憂勞庶績，矜育黔首，三面解羅，萬方引咎。

translations.literal: He worried and labored over the myriad tasks, cherished and nurtured the black-haired heads; on three sides he loosened the nets, and from the myriad regions blame was drawn to himself.
translations.idiomatic: He toiled over every duty of state, nurtured the common people, opened the nets on three sides, and took blame upon himself from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 納民軌物，驅時仁壽，神化隆平，生靈熙阜。

translations.literal: He brought the people within measure and things, drove the age toward benevolence and longevity; divine transformation made grain abundant, and living spirits flourished and grew rich.
translations.idiomatic: He brought the people within law and custom, led the age toward benevolence and long life; his transforming power made harvests rich and the people prosper.

sentences.zh: 虔心恭己，奉天事地，協氣橫流，休徵紹至。

translations.literal: With reverent heart he disciplined himself, served heaven and honored earth; harmonious qi flowed across, and auspicious signs came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: With reverent heart he governed himself, served heaven and earth; harmony spread abroad, and good omens followed one upon another.

sentences.zh: 壇場望幸，雲亭虛位，推而不居，聖道彌粹。

translations.literal: The altar and ritual ground awaited his presence; Cloud Pavilion stood with empty seat; he pushed forward yet did not occupy it—the sage Way grew ever purer.
translations.idiomatic: The altar awaited him, Cloud Pavilion stood empty; he yielded and would not ascend—the sage Way grew ever purer.

sentences.zh: 齊跡姬文，登發嗣聖，道類漢光，傳莊寶命。

translations.literal: He matched the footsteps of Ji Wen, ascended and sent forth the succeeding sage; his Way resembled Han's Guangwu, transmitting the solemn precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He walked in the steps of King Wen of Zhou, raised up the sage who followed; his Way was like Guangwu of Han, passing on the sacred mandate.

sentences.zh: 知來藏往，玄覽幽鏡，鼎業靈長，洪基隆盛。

translations.literal: Knowing what was to come and storing what had passed, with dark vision and a hidden mirror; the tripod enterprise was spiritually enduring, the great foundation lofty and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the future and held the past, saw with heaven's mirror; his house was enduring, his foundation vast and bright.

sentences.zh: 崆峒問道，汾射窅然，禦辯遐逝，乘雲上仙。

translations.literal: At Kongtong he inquired of the Way; at Fen he shot and vanished into distance; his imperial chariot passed far away, riding clouds to ascend as immortal.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yellow Emperor sought the Way at Kongtong, as Yao vanished by the Fen—his imperial carriage passed beyond, riding the clouds to heaven.

sentences.zh: 哀纏率土，痛感穹玄，流澤萬葉，用教百年。

translations.literal: Grief wound through all the realm, pain reached to the vaulted dark; his flowing grace would last ten thousand generations, his teaching serve a hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Grief bound the whole land, sorrow touched heaven itself; his bounty flows through ten thousand generations, his teaching for a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 尚想睿圖，永惟聖則，道洽幽顯，仁沾動植。

translations.literal: We still recall his wise design, forever keep his sage rule; his Way pervaded hidden and manifest, his benevolence touched moving things and plants.
translations.idiomatic: We still ponder his wise design, forever hold his sacred example; his Way reached hidden and visible realms, his kindness touched all that live and grow.

sentences.zh: 爻象不陳，乾坤將息，微臣作頌，用申罔極。

translations.literal: The hexagram lines are no longer set forth; heaven and earth are about to rest; this humble minister composes the eulogy to express boundless grief.
translations.idiomatic: The oracle is stilled, heaven and earth fall silent; this humble servant writes the eulogy to voice grief beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之不悅，顧謂蘇威曰：「道衡致美先朝，此《魚藻》之義也。」

translations.literal: The emperor read it and was not pleased; he turned and said to Su Wei: "Daoheng lavishes praise on the former court—this is the meaning of 'Fish and Waterweeds.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and was displeased; turning to Su Wei he said, "Daoheng heaps praise on the former reign—this is the sense of the 'Fish and Waterweeds' ode."

sentences.zh: 於是拜司隸大夫，將置之罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed him Director of the Capital District and was about to punish him with a capital offense.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he appointed him Director of the Capital District and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 道衡不悟。

translations.literal: Daoheng did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng did not perceive his meaning.

sentences.zh: 司隸刺史房彥謙素相善，知必及禍，勸之杜絕賓客，卑辭下氣，而道衡不能用。

translations.literal: Fang Yanqian, Inspector of the Capital Region, had long been on good terms with him and, knowing disaster must come, urged him to cut off visitors and speak with humble, submissive words—but Daoheng would not follow the advice.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yanqian, Inspector of the Capital Region, was an old friend who saw calamity coming and urged him to shut his doors to guests and speak humbly—but Daoheng would not listen.

sentences.zh: 會議新令，久不能決，道衡謂朝士曰：「向使高熲不死，令決當久行。」

translations.literal: When the court debated a new ordinance and could not decide for a long time, Daoheng said to the officials, "If only Gao Jiong had not died, this ordinance would surely have been long in force."
translations.idiomatic: During a prolonged debate over a new ordinance, Daoheng told his colleagues, "Had Gao Jiong still lived, this measure would already be firmly in place."

sentences.zh: 有人奏之，帝怒曰：「汝憶高熲邪？」

translations.literal: Someone reported this; the emperor said in anger, "Do you miss Gao Jiong?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported him; the emperor raged, "Are you pining for Gao Jiong?"

sentences.zh: 付執法者勘之。

translations.literal: He handed him over to the law officers for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He turned him over to the judicial authorities for investigation.

sentences.zh: 道衡自以非大過，促憲司早斷。

translations.literal: Daoheng thought the offense was not grave and urged the judicial office to decide quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng assumed the fault was minor and pressed the court to rule promptly.

sentences.zh: 暨于奏日，冀帝赦之，敕家人具饌，以備賓客來候者。

translations.literal: When the day of judgment came he hoped the emperor would pardon him and ordered his household to prepare food for guests who might come to visit.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sentencing he still hoped for pardon and told his household to prepare a feast for friends who might call.

sentences.zh: 及奏，帝令自盡。

translations.literal: When the report was made, the emperor ordered him to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When the verdict was reported, the emperor ordered him to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 道衡殊不意，未能引訣。

translations.literal: Daoheng had not expected this at all and could not bring himself to take leave of life.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng was utterly unprepared and could not bring himself to bid farewell.

sentences.zh: 憲司重奏，縊而殺之，妻子徙且末。

translations.literal: The judicial office reported again; he was strangled to death, and his wife and children were banished to Qimo.
translations.idiomatic: The court reported again; he was strangled, and his wife and children were exiled to Qimo.

sentences.zh: 時年七十。

translations.literal: He was then seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy at the time.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under heaven considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The empire regarded his death as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 有集七十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He left a collection of writings in seventy juan, which circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to seventy juan and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 有子五人，收最知名，出繼族父孺。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Shou was the most famous, having been given in adoption to his clansman-father Ru.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons; Shou was the best known, having been adopted by his kinsman Ru.

sentences.zh: 孺清貞孤介，不交流俗，涉歷經史，有才思，雖不為大文，所有詩詠，詞致清遠。

translations.literal: Ru was pure, upright, and aloof, mixing little with the vulgar world; he ranged through the classics and histories and had literary talent; though he did not write major works, his poems were clear and far-reaching in diction.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was upright and solitary, shunning vulgar company; versed in the classics and histories, he possessed literary gifts; though he wrote no major pieces, his poems were lucid and refined.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為侍御史、揚州總管司功參軍。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he served as Attending Censor and Recorder of the Yangzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he served as Attending Censor and Recorder under the Yangzhou Area Command.

sentences.zh: 每以方直自處，府僚多不便之。

translations.literal: He always conducted himself with square integrity, which many colleagues in the prefecture found inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: He always held himself to strict integrity, which many colleagues in the prefectural staff found awkward.

sentences.zh: 及滿，轉清陽令、襄城郡掾，卒官。

translations.literal: When his term ended he became Magistrate of Qingyang and Assistant of Xiangcheng Commandery, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he became Magistrate of Qingyang and aide in Xiangcheng Commandery, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 所經並有惠政。

translations.literal: Every post he held showed benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he left benevolent rule behind.

sentences.zh: 與道衡偏相友愛，收初生，即與孺為後，養於孺宅。

translations.literal: He was especially close to Daoheng; when Shou was born he was at once given to Ru as heir and raised in Ru's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to Daoheng; as soon as Shou was born he was given to Ru as heir and raised in Ru's home.

sentences.zh: 至於成長，殆不識本生。

translations.literal: By the time he grew up he scarcely knew his birth parents.
translations.idiomatic: By adulthood he scarcely knew his birth parents.

sentences.zh: 太常丞胡仲操曾在朝堂，就孺借刀子割爪甲。

translations.literal: Hu Zhongcao, Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, once in court asked Ru to lend him a knife to trim his fingernails.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhongcao, an aide in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, once asked Ru in court to lend him a knife to trim his nails.

sentences.zh: 孺以仲操非雅士，竟不與之。

translations.literal: Ru considered Zhongcao no man of refinement and in the end would not give it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru judged Zhongcao no gentleman of taste and refused him outright.

sentences.zh: 其不肯妄交，清介獨行，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His refusal to make casual acquaintances and his pure, solitary conduct were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His refusal of casual acquaintance and his austere, solitary ways were all of this sort.

sentences.zh: 道衡兄子邁，官至選部郎，從父弟道實，官至禮部侍郎、離石太守，並知名於世。

translations.literal: Daoheng's elder brother's son Mai rose to Selection Department Gentleman; his cousin Daoshi became Vice Minister of Rites and Administrator of Lishi—both were renowned in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng's nephew Mai rose to a post in the Selection Department; his cousin Daoshi became Vice Minister of Rites and Administrator of Lishi—both won fame in their day.

sentences.zh: 從子德音，有雋才，起家為游騎尉。

translations.literal: His nephew Deyin had outstanding talent and first entered office as Cavalry Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Deyin possessed outstanding talent and began his career as Cavalry Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 佐魏澹修《魏史》，史成，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He assisted Wei Dan in compiling the History of Wei; when the history was completed he was promoted to Assistant Editor.
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Wei Dan in compiling the History of Wei and, when the work was finished, was promoted to Assistant Editor.

sentences.zh: 及越王侗稱制東都，王世充之僭號也，軍書羽檄，皆出其手。

translations.literal: When Prince Yue of Dong assumed regency in the eastern capital and Wang Shichong usurped the throne, military dispatches and urgent proclamations all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yue of Dong held regency in the eastern capital and Wang Shichong seized the throne, all military orders and urgent proclamations issued from his pen.

sentences.zh: 世充平，以罪伏誅。

translations.literal: When Shichong was overthrown, he was executed for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong fell, he was executed for his offenses.

sentences.zh: 所有文筆，多行于時。

translations.literal: His writings, many of them, circulated widely in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his writings circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：二三子有齊之季，皆以辭藻著聞，爰曆周、隋，鹹見推重。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: These two or three men, in the late age of Qi, all became famous for their literary ornament; through Zhou and Sui alike they were esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In the last days of Qi these men all won fame for literary brilliance; through Zhou and Sui alike they were held in high regard.

sentences.zh: 李稱一代俊偉，薛則時之令望，握靈蛇以俱照，騁逸足以並驅，文雅縱橫，金聲玉振。

translations.literal: Li was called the outstanding genius of an age, Xue the leading hope of the time; each grasped the spirit serpent and shone together, each galloped with equal speed; their literary grace ranged far, their voices rang like gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: Li was hailed as the age's towering talent, Xue as its leading hope; each wielded the brush like a spirit serpent, each kept pace in swift excellence; their prose ranged freely, their voices rang clear as gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 靜言揚榷，盧居二子之右。

translations.literal: Speaking calmly and weighing merits, Lu stands to the right of these two.
translations.idiomatic: On calm reflection, Lu ranks above the other two.

sentences.zh: 李、薛紆青拖紫，思道官途寥落，雖窮通有命，抑亦不護細行之所致也。

translations.literal: Li and Xue wore purple and green sashes, while Sidao's official path was desolate; though fortune and failure have fate, this too came from his failure to guard small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue rose to high office in purple and green, while Sidao's career languished; though fortune has its decree, this also came of his neglect of small proprieties.
